LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Imagn Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. Pick: Packers 31, Panthers 24 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Green Bay fell to 4-3 with a loss to Detroit in Week 7, and it's in last place in a loaded NFC North through seven weeks. Meanwhile, the Panthers (3-3) are in first place in the NFC South despite a major blowout loss at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Carolina made the playoffs in the 2025 season, but it has a ton of injuries on both sides of the ball that make it a tough team to trust against other quality opponents -- like Green Bay. Oddsmakers agree with that sentiment, as they've set the Packers as favorites at home to open this week. Panthers vs. Packers Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Panthers +3.5 (-110) Packers -3.5 (-110) Panthers: +154 Packers: -185 48.5 (Over -105/Under -115) There hasn't been a ton of movement in the odds for this game , as the Packers remain 3.5-point favorites at home. The total has jumped up from 47.5 to 48.5 while the moneyline has actually moved in Carolina's favor. According to DraftKings, just 22 percent of the moneyline bets and 41 percent of the spread bets are on the Panthers after their Week 7 showing against Tampa Bay. Earlier this week, I shared in SI Betting's preview for this game why I believe Green Bay is a worthwhile bet: The Panthers’ run defense was torched in Week 7 by Tampa Bay, and this could be a “get-right” spot for Matt LaFleur’s offense. Love should be able to attack through the air, as the Panthers are a below-average defense overall (20th in EPA/Play), and they entered Week 7 allowing the most yards per carry in the league. Meanwhile, Green Bay’s defense held a vaunted Detroit offense to just 20 points and is now fifth in the league in EPA/Play. If it weren’t for multiple missed field goals, the Pack could be entering this game with a 5-2 record. Carolina beat Detroit this season, but it has some confounding losses against Cleveland and at home against Tampa Bay. I don’t love this team – which is extremely banged up after Taylor Moton went down in Week 7 – on a short week against a Packers squad that has an above-average defense. I’m going to lay the points with a Green Bay team that needs this game a lot more than Carolina does if it’s going to make the playoffs. I'm not the only member of the SI Betting team taking Green Bay, as Iain MacMillan shared in his Road to 272 column -- where he bets on every NFL game, every week -- why he likes the Pack at home as well: I wrote about how I was out on the Panthers last week, and I proved to be right as they ended up on the wrong side of a blowout against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. I'm still out on this Panthers team, as they seem like a significant regression candidate after a strong start to the season. Bryce Young, up until last week, had been playing leaps and bounds better than he had the previous three seasons, and I'm of the belief that it's more of a sign of an abnormally strong start against some bad defenses as opposed to a quarterback who improved by tenfold in a single offseason. The Packers' defense ranks 12th in opponent EPA per play and 10th in opponent EPA per dropback, so with them being on their home field on a short week, I expect them to get to Young in this game. The vibes were so high and the Panthers were favored at home before dropping the egg of all eggs against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Now, a loss puts them below .500, souring what had been a really fun start to the season. Will they lose? Here's what the early odds say for this primetime bout. The Panthers are +160 to win outright, and the Packers are -192 on the moneyline. The oddsmakers don't have a lot of faith in the Panthers, despite both teams coming off a loss. The Panthers just can't get healthy. Taylor Moton went down shortly after returning, and they're still without Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn. Meanwhile, the Packers are adding players. So, unfortunately, there are plenty of reasons to expect the Panthers to lose, and it's unlikely they can replicate last season's magical upset. The same formula simply won't work, and the Packers will likely not underestimate them this time. away.blurb: The Packers didn’t designate Micah Parsons for return this week because the team doesn’t actually practice this week, which would mean one-third of his 21-day return-to-play window would have been wasted. Receiver Matthew Golden (shoulder and foot) did not practice. Along with Christian Watson, Golden is the driving force in the passing game. Without him, the Packers would be incredibly shorthanded in terms of passing-game playmakers. There was some good news, though. Defensive tackles Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and Anthony Campbell (ankle) would not have practiced on Monday but would have been limited on Tuesday. Campbell was one of the standouts against Detroit. Still a DNP was Phillips, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract in free agency this past offseason. He has 2.5 sacks in five games but was inactive last week against Tampa Bay. Limited participation: G Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), edge Brenton Cox (quad), DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle). Packers-Lions Final Injury Report: Zaire Franklin Out; Backups Thrown Into Fire GREEN BAY, Wis. – As is typically the case for a Thursday night game, the Green Bay Packers will be a banged-up bunch for their game against the Carolina Panthers. The Packers held a walk-through practice on Tuesday. If they would have practiced, they would have been down four starters. One of them was Travis Glover, who has started the past four games at right guard. More on that and the injury report in a moment. But first, there was a potential big update on the status of Micah Parsons. “I sure hope so,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Wednesday evening. There was a touch of optimism there, though LaFleur was quick to remind that it will be a medical decision before the superstar pass rusher returns to practice. “I’m itching for it, though, for sure,” LaFleur said. Will Kevin Zeitler Start at Right Guard? Glover is dealing with a knee injury and didn’t play particularly well against the Lions. If he’s not ready, will Kevin Zeitler make his long-awaited debut? Zeitler was inactive against Detroit and has played only on special teams in his two appearances. “If we need him, absolutely,” LaFleur said when asked if Zeitler is ready to contribute on offense. “I think he's done a nice job. Here's a guy that came in and didn't have an offseason, didn't have training camp, and he's kind of gradually working his way back into it.” Good News and Bad News for Packers Linebacker Zaire Franklin would not have practiced due to the shin injury sustained at practice last week and will not be ready for Thursday, LaFleur said. That means a secon consecutie week for Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper. “I sure hope so,” LaFleur said when asked about Golden’s availability, “but we're still kind of working through it. You're not getting any real reps. Everything's pretty much walk-through. We will have a short indy [individual drills period] tomorrow, but to move guys around and see how they look, but certainly hopeful for him.”

The Carolina Panthers are looking to bounce back from a Week 7 loss as they share the field Thursday against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field in Green Bay. Carolina got some good news heading into that matchup, with wide receiver Jalen Coker practicing in full on Tuesday, according to the team’s latest injury report. Carolina’s attack was grounded as a whole in that contest by Tampa Bay, and it will be aiming to bounce back this Thursday in Titletown. It was an embarrassing performance for the Panthers at home, allowing Tampa Bay to do whatever they wanted in that game. Carolina left the game 3-3 and having a lot of questions still to be answered. The good news? They have a quick turnaround as they will head to Green Bay to face off against the Packers. The bad news? Green Bay is a good team and the Panthers will enter this game banged up. As the team returned to the practice field for a walk-through on Monday, there were some notable names on the injury report. The most notable additions are on the offensive side of the football with guard Damien Lewis and Jalen Coker. Lewis was added to the injury report with a knee injury. He missed the Detroit game with an elbow injury but returned to play against both Philadelphia and Tampa Bay. Now, a knee injury could limit his ability all week and his chances to play at Green Bay. If the Panthers are without Lewis, it would put a bit of a dent into the Panthers' offensive line, one that is already missing Taylor Moton , who went on injured reserve Monday. Losing another starter could be a disaster, especially with a good Packers' pass rush on tap. Coker has a shoulder injury which will limit him a bit this week. The Panthers are going to need to be healthy on offense so that Green Bay can't just key in on Tetairoa McMillan all game long. In addition to those two, here is the full injury report which was an estimation based on the walk through: QB Bryce Young (knee) | Monday: Full Phillips missed Week 7 with a hamstring injury. away.headline: Bucs-Panthers Inactives | Baker Mayfield Returns to Action
away.blurb: After missing three games due to a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand, quarterback Baker Mayfield is back in the lineup for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday as they take on the Carolina Panthers in a critical intra-division game. Mayfield carried a questionable designation on the injury report into the weekend but was able to practice without limitations throughout the week. He intends to wear a specialized glove on his right hand that offers added support to the injured joint, preventing the thumb from being bent backward. Mayfield will not have the team's top receiving target at his disposal, however, as wide receiver Emeka Egbuka is out for Week Seven with both a concussion and a foot injury. In addition, starting right tackle Luke Goedeke is out due to a calf ailment and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. will miss his third straight outing thanks to a rib fracture. The Buccaneers and Panthers submitted their list of inactives at 11:32 a.m. ET on Sunday, 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff of their Week Seven meeting at Bank of America Stadium. After elevating linebacker Caden Fordham from the practice squad, the Buccaneers had 54 available players and thus had to name six inactives to get down to the game-day limit of 48. The Panthers also elevated outside linebacker Nick Hampton and cornerback Robert Rochell from the practice squad and had to name seven inactive players. Carolina will be without one of its top pass-rushers as Jaelan Phillips is out due to a hamstring strain. Fellow outside linebacker Thomas Incoom is also unavailable due to a calf issue, and he was placed on injured reserve on Saturday. away.headline: Carolina Panthers vs. Bucs: Who wins? Our predictions, injury report, TV info
away.blurb: So can the Panthers sustain their recent success? Will Mayfield’s return yield a new hope? Will the NFC South standings be shaken up? Fans can also check the game out on radio: WRFX The Fox, 99.7 FM. Anish Shroff (play-by-play), Luke Kuechly (analyst), Jake Delhomme (analyst), Jim Szoke (host), Kristen Balboni (sideline). For full local listings, check out the Carolina Panthers Radio Network . Special note: Kuechly will receive his Pro Football Hall of Fame ring at halftime of the game in Bank of America Stadium. Out: OLB Thomas Incoom (calf), OLB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) Questionable: OT Monroe Freeling (knee), LB Bam Martin-Scott (hamstring) Out: WR Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot), OT Luke Goedeke (calf), S Antoine Winfield (rib) Questionable: QB Baker Mayfield (right thumb) Alex Zietlow: Panthers 35, Bucs 31. I know that Baker Mayfield’s almost-certain return will make this Bucs offense more dynamic. And I know that scoring 35 on this Bucs team will be difficult, considering their opportunistic defensive backfield and their Top 5 rush defense. Still, barring an implosion of turnovers, I think the Panthers outscore and outlast a Bucs team trying to get back on track. Can the Carolina Panthers make it three wins in a row? And can the Tampa Bay Buccaneers get back on track? The Panthers (3-2) are returning to Bank of America Stadium for their Week 7 contest (1 p.m., FOX) fresh off two statement victories against the Detroit Lions and the Philadelphia Eagles . They’re looking to go 4-2 for the first time as a franchise since 2019 and start 2-0 in the NFC South for the first time since 2022. Carolina ranks first in the NFL in passing yards per game (295.6), second in total yards per game (404.4) and fourth in points per game (29.2). And its defense — minus the Week 1 fiasco against the Bears that’s looking more and more like an aberration — is Top 10 in several statistics, including rushing yards allowed. The Panthers have allowed fewer than 50 yards in each of the last two weeks: 46 against the Lions, 35 against the Eagles. It’s true that the defense is a bit affected by injury, specifically at the outside linebacker spot with no Jaelan Phillips or Thomas Incoom this week . It’s also true that the defense has only had to play against starting quarterbacks three times so far this season, and two of those three — against Caleb Williams of the Bears and Deshaun Watson of the Browns — have yielded losses. That won’t happen this week; it looks like the Bucs will be led by Baker Mayfield, who’s missed the last few weeks with a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand. Speaking of the Bucs (1-5): While many of their offensive stats might be skewed by Mayfield’s absence, many of their strengths will remain. Namely? Their rush defense. Tampa Bay ranks second in the NFL in rush yards allowed per game at 75.5, thanks to a defensive line anchored by nose tackle Vita Vea and an entire unit led by rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter. away.headline: Carolina Panthers: Taylor Moton suffers injury in loss to Tampa Bay
away.blurb: Canales also confirmed that Moton would be out for a while now with the fracture in that fibula, so the Panthers are going to have to find another solution. You could see the frustration on Canales' face and hear it in his voice as he said he was sick for Moton and how hard he worked back to get on the field and help his team. Moton made his debut last week coming out of the bye against the Philadelphia Eagles after being sidelined by blood clots. The Panthers' offense was riding a hot streak going into this game but it was clear that Tampa Bay had done their homework. They limited Bryce Young all game long and forced two takeaways from the quarterback, getting pressure through the line early and often in the game. Carolina will have a quick turnaround in Week 8 as they head to Green Bay to face off against the Packers on Thursday Night Football. The game will kickoff at 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime. It will be a good test for the Panthers' line that will feature the return of Moton. Carolina Panthers: Taylor Moton suffers injury in loss to Tampa Bay PantherRoundtable 174 Members • 1,437 Posts PantherRoundtable PantherRoundtable Related stories REUTERS REUTERS Carolina Panthers Have Tough Injury Update After Loss Zack Pearson Partner Oct 26, 2026 3:03 AM Published Oct 26, 2026 3:03 AM The Carolina Panthers had a really tough injury update to provide for an offensive tackle. The Carolina Panthers saw their two-game win streak end at the hands of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Tampa Bay came into Charlotte and beat the Panthers 43-13 , dominating from start to finish. It sent the Panthers to 3-3 and cut their lead in the NFC South to just a half game to the Atlanta Falcons. More importantly, it showcased some potential weaknesses for other teams to expose moving forward. One area the Panthers are going to have to sure up their play is at offensive line. But that is going to be a little tougher now. Offensive tackle Taylor Moton left Sunday's game early on a cart. It was a tough feeling for Panthers' fans to see their starting right tackle go down and after the game, head coach Dave Canales confirmed he suffered an ankle and fibula injury. It was thought of as a huge boost to the line, matching him up with Rasheed Walker. Now, the Panthers are really going to have to find a way to make it work and it will likely be rookie Monroe Freeling , who has started games already earlier this season. If the Panthers want to make a run this season, they are going to rely on that offense and that starts with the offensive line.

home.headline: Packers-Panthers Tuesday injury report: Time near for Micah Parsons, Kevin Zeitler?
home.blurb: The Packers didn’t designate Micah Parsons for return this week because the team doesn’t actually practice this week, which would mean one-third of his 21-day return-to-play window would have been wasted. Receiver Matthew Golden (shoulder and foot) did not practice. Along with Christian Watson, Golden is the driving force in the passing game. Without him, the Packers would be incredibly shorthanded in terms of passing-game playmakers. There was some good news, though. Defensive tackles Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and Anthony Campbell (ankle) would not have practiced on Monday but would have been limited on Tuesday. Campbell was one of the standouts against Detroit. Still a DNP was Phillips, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract in free agency this past offseason. He has 2.5 sacks in five games but was inactive last week against Tampa Bay. Limited participation: G Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), edge Brenton Cox (quad), DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle). Packers-Lions Final Injury Report: Zaire Franklin Out; Backups Thrown Into Fire GREEN BAY, Wis. – As is typically the case for a Thursday night game, the Green Bay Packers will be a banged-up bunch for their game against the Carolina Panthers. The Packers held a walk-through practice on Tuesday. If they would have practiced, they would have been down four starters. One of them was Travis Glover, who has started the past four games at right guard. More on that and the injury report in a moment. But first, there was a potential big update on the status of Micah Parsons. “I sure hope so,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Wednesday evening. There was a touch of optimism there, though LaFleur was quick to remind that it will be a medical decision before the superstar pass rusher returns to practice. “I’m itching for it, though, for sure,” LaFleur said. Will Kevin Zeitler Start at Right Guard? Glover is dealing with a knee injury and didn’t play particularly well against the Lions. If he’s not ready, will Kevin Zeitler make his long-awaited debut? Zeitler was inactive against Detroit and has played only on special teams in his two appearances. “If we need him, absolutely,” LaFleur said when asked if Zeitler is ready to contribute on offense. “I think he's done a nice job. Here's a guy that came in and didn't have an offseason, didn't have training camp, and he's kind of gradually working his way back into it.” Good News and Bad News for Packers Linebacker Zaire Franklin would not have practiced due to the shin injury sustained at practice last week and will not be ready for Thursday, LaFleur said. That means a secon consecutie week for Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper. “I sure hope so,” LaFleur said when asked about Golden’s availability, “but we're still kind of working through it. You're not getting any real reps. Everything's pretty much walk-through. We will have a short indy [individual drills period] tomorrow, but to move guys around and see how they look, but certainly hopeful for him.”

home.headline: Panthers’ Jalen Coker injury update is great news for TNF vs. Packers
home.blurb: Coker was a limited practice participant on Monday, sparking fears about his chances to play against the Packers due to a shoulder injury. While he’s not yet removed from the injury report, he’s now widely expected to eventually get cleared to see action versus Green Bay. The Carolina Panthers are looking to bounce back from a Week 7 loss as they share the field Thursday against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field in Green Bay. Carolina got some good news heading into that matchup, with wide receiver Jalen Coker practicing in full on Tuesday, according to the team’s latest injury report. The 24-year-old Coker is coming off a letdown performance. After racking up 97 receiving yards on six receptions and 13 targets in a 25-14 win on the road over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6, the former Holy Cross Crusaders star caught only one of four targets for nine receiving yards in a 43-13 demolition at the hands of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a Week 7 game on Sunday at home. Carolina’s attack was grounded as a whole in that contest by Tampa Bay, and it will be aiming to bounce back this Thursday in Titletown. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Coker is the other half of the Panthers’ top downfield duo in 2026 alongside wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan. On the season, Coker is second on the team with 328 receiving yards to go along with two touchdowns on 25 receptions and 39 targets. McMillan leads the Panthers with 511 receiving yards and two scores on 36 catches and 55 targets. As a team, the Bryce Young-led passing game of Carolina is second overall in the league with an average of 276.0 yards per outing. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. home.headline: Packers injury report: Jordan Love upgraded, 2 defensive starters added
home.blurb: Love, who is dealing with back soreness coming out of last Sunday's win over the Dallas Cowboys, got in a full padded practice on Thursday. He said Wednesday that he had no concerns over his availability for Sunday's showdown with the Detroit Lions , and Love's upgraded practice status on Thursday appears to confirm his belief. Barring a setback, he'll start against the Lions at Ford Field. Two defensive starters are dealing with new issues: Franklin has a shin injury, while Van Ness has an illness. It's currently unclear if either player is in danger of missing Sunday. More information will be available come Friday, when Matt LaFleur answers questions from the media before practice and before the Packers release a final injury report. Last week, safety Evan Williams was able to get through an illness and play well against the Cowboys. The only player who did not participate for the Packers at practice on Thursday was receiver Bo Melton, who is dealing with a back injury. He can be assumed out for Sunday unless he practices in some capacity on Friday. Receivers Christian Watson (ankle) and Matthew Golden (shoulder) both practiced in a limited capacity. LaFleur said both would play Sunday against the Lions. Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DL Anthony Campbell (ankle), CB Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), LB Zaire Franklin (shin), WR Matthew Golden (shoulder), DL Jordon Riley (Achilles), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), EDGE Lukas Van Ness (illness), WR Christian Watson (ankle), WR Savion Williams (ankle) Packers updated Week 7 injury report, Thursday Full participation: QB Jordan Love (back) Did not participate: WR Bo Melton (back) A final injury report for both teams will arrive on Friday afternoon. On Tuesday, the Packers released their latest injury report, showing wide receiver Matthew Golden missing practice for the second straight day due to foot and shoulder issues. It is important to note, however, that Green Bay didn't actually practice on the field and just held a walkthrough on Tuesday. The former Texas Longhorns star wide receiver is in the middle of a breakout season, becoming one of the most reliable downfield weapons for quarterback Jordan Love in a Green Bay offense that is fifth in the league overall with an average of 268.6 passing yards per game. With only a day for practice left before the showdown against the Panthers at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Golden will have to show up and practice on Wednesday to allay some fears about his chances to see action in Week 8. There has been a ton of reporting around Jackson's ankle injury that has kept him sidelined since the second half of Week 4, but NFL insider Ian Rapoport shared on Tuesday that Jackson is expected to play in Sunday's marquee matchup against Josh Allen. From @BigDayESPN : #Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is expected to return to the field this week. That, plus a little more on his fun press conference. pic.twitter.com/AKQSjjAy5U "I expect, based on the people I've spoke with, that Lamar Jackson will play this week," Rapoport said. "He'll be on the field this week against the Buffalo Bills. I know we've been here before. This is a two-to-three week injury. He is through the third week. He is believed to be as close to 100 percent as he has been, and the Ravens do expect him to play." Jackson's potential return has already caused a shift in the odds for this game at DraftKings Sportsbook . Baltimore opened as a 3.5-point underdog in this AFC showdown, but the line has already shifted to Ravens +3 ahead of their practice on Wednesday. It could move down further if Jackson logs a full practice. The two-time league MVP returned to practice ahead of the team's Week 7 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, logging limited sessions before being ruled out. Jackson was originally questionable for the game, but the Ravens ruled him out on Saturday, forcing Tyler Huntley to make his third start of the season. The Ravens (4-3) are in last place in the AFC North after back-to-back losses against division opponents, and they're just 7-13 all-time when Jackson is out. So, they need the star quarterback to return for a matchup with the 5-1 Bills, who are looking to earn the top spot in the AFC this season. In his four games this season, Jackson completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score. For now, it appears the two-time MVP is on track to play against Buffalo. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Bills (5-1). Coming off their bye week, Josh Allen and the Bills lead the AFC East by a game and a half over the Patriots. The Ravens, meanwhile, have lost their last two and currently sit in the cellar in the AFC North. Two optimistic notes for the visiting Ravens. First and most important, Lamar Jackson is expected back under center for Baltimore. Second, the Ravens have been much better away from home this season with three wins in four games away from M&T Bank Stadium. Baltimore arrives in Buffalo coming off its worst loss of the season, a 35-13 home defeat to Cincinnati. Tyler Huntley started in place of the injured Jackson and completed 23 of 34 passes for a career-high 298 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Zay Flowers produced eight catches for 137 yards and a 48-yard touchdown. The issue was on the defensive side of the ball. The Ravens allowed the Bengals to rack up 357 total yards of offense. The true difference-maker was in the red zone. Cincinnati was in the red zone five times last Sunday…and scored touchdowns each of the five times. Buffalo, meanwhile, enters rested after a Week 8 bye and riding a two-game winning streak. The Bills’ most recent game was a 33-30 road victory over Las Vegas on October 18, following a 37-34 win over the Rams the previous week. Josh Allen remains the centerpiece of one of the NFL’s most explosive attacks, entering Sunday with 1,504 passing yards and nine touchdown passes while also leading Buffalo with eight rushing touchdowns. James Cook has added 627 rushing yards, helping the Bills average 148.8 yards per game on the ground, second in the NFL. away.headline: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson expected to play in Week 8: report
away.blurb: Jackson was able to notch limited practice participation leading up to this past Sunday’s Week 7 loss to the Bengals, but he was ultimately ruled out. Now, the Ravens are gearing up for a highly-anticipated Week 8 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has missed each of the last three games after suffering an ankle injury in Week 4. The Ravens are 1-2 over that span with Tyler Huntley at the helm, dropping each of their last two games against the division-rival Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. On Tuesday, NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport confidently reported that Jackson will be on the field for this Week 8 clash. “I expect, based on the people that I’ve spoken with, that Lamar Jackson will play this week. He will be on the field this week against the Buffalo Bills,” Rapoport said. “I know we’ve been here before. This was a 2-3 week injury — he’s through the third week. He is believed to be as close to 100% as he has been and the Ravens do expect him to play.” With Jackson off the field, the Ravens have dropped to last place in the AFC North standings with a 4-3 record. They’ll look to get back in the win column in a difficult road matchup against the Bills this coming Sunday. Sunday’s game will kick off at 1 p.m. ET. The Ravens then have a short week to prepare for a “Thursday Night Football” matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 9. away.blurb: Ravens Week 7 Injury Report: Lamar Jackson Officially Limited - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Colts WR Josh Downs reportedly wants out amid fire sale Ravens Week 7 Injury Report: Lamar Jackson Officially Limited Despite quarterback Lamar Jackson not practicing during the media portion of practice, he apparently did some limited work. As stated above, Jackson practiced in a limited fashion . Head coach Jesse Minter also said the quarterback did some work with the team as well. Jackson was officially limited with his ankle. Whether or not that means he can play on Sunday remains to be seen. The good news for the Ravens is that the passer was limited, as opposed to not practicing. Wide receiver Rashod Bateman (shoulder), safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee), tight end Matthew Hibner (hand), guard Vega Ioane (ankle), guard John Simpson (groin), tackle Ronnie Stanley (rest, toe, ankle), cornerback T.J. Tampa (knee), guard Andrew Vorhees (foot), and defensive lineman Broderick Washington (ankle) were all limited. If Ioane's ankle leads to him being ruled out, it would lead to Vorhees potentially taking over. However, Vorhees is also dealing with a foot injury that has led to him missing the last two games. If the worst-case scenario happens for the Ravens' line, it would be Emery Jones Jr. stepping in yet again as the team's right guard. Jones has filled in with Ioane stepping in at center and Vorhees being out due to injury. TRENDING Rays rally, avoid sweep (Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images) James Brizuela Thu, October 22, 2026 at 3:37 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens are gearing up to face the Cincinnati Bengals, and the team has released its initial injury report. The full injury report is as follows: The only two players who did not participate on Wednesday is veteran defensive lineman Calais Campbell, who had veteran rest, and linebacker Tavius Robinson, who is dealing with a pectoral injury. Hibner has returned to practice after missing Week 6 due to a hand injury. A bigger issue is Ioane appearing on the injury report with an ankle ailment. He has served as the team's emergency center, but it does appear that Cam Jurgens is returning. Jurgens did not have a red no-contact jersey on at practice, and Minter stated the team is "excited" to get him on the field as the team's center. If Jurgens can line up as the team's center, that would lead to Ioane returning to the right guard position. This is assuming that Ioane can also suit up. Some better news is that Tampa is also working his way back from injury. The cornerback suffered a knee injury in Week 1 that has sidelined him since then. Baltimore has an important matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals. Losing two divisional matchups might come back to haunt the Ravens at the end of the season.

home.blurb: The Bills come out of their Week 7 bye hoping to get wide receiver D.J. Moore and defensive tackle Ed Oliver back after both missed the previous two games. He did not practice Wednesday or Thursday before the Raiders game but returned on a limited basis Friday and was listed as questionable. Buffalo ultimately kept him inactive. He missed five consecutive practices before returning on a limited basis the Friday before the Raiders game. Oliver was listed as questionable but inactive in Las Vegas. Dalton Kincaid left Buffalo's victory over Las Vegas because of a rib injury but was able to return. The Bills listed him as questionable to return. Kincaid came back in the fourth quarter and caught a 14-yard pass three plays later. Chubb went out during the second quarter and was initially listed as questionable. He returned later in the first half and played 21 of Buffalo's 66 defensive snaps against Las Vegas. T.J. Sanders played against Las Vegas and recorded one tackle after being listed as questionable because of a shoulder injury. His suspension begins Oct. 26 and he can return to Buffalo's active roster Nov. 2, meaning he will miss Sunday's game against Baltimore. picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Bengals in Week 8, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Heading into Week, the 1-6 Tennessee Titans have everything to prove, but also nothing at all. Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. picks.headline: Titans scouting report vs Cincinnati Bengals, matchups, prediction NFL Week 8
picks.blurb: News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals TITANS Titans scouting report vs Cincinnati Bengals, matchups, prediction NFL Week 8 Tyler Palmateer Nashville Tennessean Oct. 28, 2026, 5:04 a.m. CT The Tennessee Titans will face the Cincinnati Bengals in NFL Week 8 following a 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns. The Bengals' passing offense, led by quarterback Joe Burrow, poses a significant challenge to the Titans' struggling defense. Positives are hard to find amid the Tennessee Titans’ struggles, but running back Tony Pollard was one last week. The Memphis native had his second-best game as a Titans player, with 129 yards rushing and three touchdowns on 25 carries in a gutting 27-24 home loss to the Cleveland Browns on Oct. 25. Maybe Pollard can do it again when the Titans (1-6) face the Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) at Paycor Stadium on Nov. 1 (noon CT, CBS) in NFL Week 8. The Bengals' and Browns ' run defenses are about the same statistically. Cincinnati allows 116.3 rushing yards per game, which ranks 19th in the league. The Titans gained a season-high 322 yards of offense with Pollard’s contributions, taking pressure off developing second-year quarterback Cam Ward . Tennessee coach Robert Saleh pinned the Browns loss on defense . Now that unit will face Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, who’s 11th in the league with 1,653 yards passing, and second with 15 passing touchdowns, to go with three interceptions. Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Browns. One Cincinnati Bengals stat to know Cincinnati has 13 pass plays of 25 yards or more this season. Tennessee has seven. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Bengals The good news: Cincinnati’s offense ranks 29th in rushing yards per game (81.2), so there’s an opportunity for the Titans to make the Bengals one-dimensional. The bad news: Cincinnati’s offense is doing fine without a rushing threat, averaging 345.2 yards. It isn’t a big Titans advantage, but they must capitalize on it and see if stopping the run allows their pass rush to play like it did against the Colts (six sacks). It will take a stark turnaround after Tennessee allowed a season-high 183 yards rushing against the Browns. That marked the franchise’s worst single-game Pro Football Focus run defense grade (36.3) since 2023. Personnel changes up front have not helped. Run-stopping defensive tackle Jordan Elliott was released on Oct. 20 after breaking the NFL's gun policy . Third-year defender Timmy Horne was signed from the practice squad to replace him. Where Cincinnati Bengals have edge vs. Titans Tennessee’s secondary tackled poorly and took bad angles against the Browns, making rookie receiver KC Concepcion look like a Pro Bowler (eight catches, 129 yards). Imagine what Burrow and receivers Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase might do. The Titans haven't seen an offense like this in 2026. The Bengals are seventh in the league in passing yards per game (264) and get 76% of their total yards through the air. Higgins and Chase have accounted for nine of the Bengals’ 13 explosive pass plays. Saleh’s also soul-searching in his secondary. Alontae Taylor was signed in the offseason to fortify one of Tennessee’s outside corner spots, but he was made inactive in Week 6 by coach’s decision and didn’t see the field in Week 7. Now it looks like Taylor will likely move to nickel . This would be a good week for Taylor to make a contribution, assuming Saleh plays him. Score prediction: Bengals 35, Titans 21 The Titans' scarred defense won’t be able to slow Burrow, and they can’t depend on Ward to keep pace in a shootout. It looks like their worst-case scenario matchup. Winning the turnover battle and making a few plays on special teams would help, but the Titans will be fortunate to keep it within 14 points. Tyler Palmateer covers the Tennessee Titans for The Tennessean. Have a story idea for Tyler? Reach him at tpalmateer@tennessean.com and on the X platform, @tpalmateer83 .

home.headline: Bengals make roster moves after Erick All injury update
home.blurb: The Cincinnati Bengals moved quickly to sign an outside player after the Erick All injury , but weren’t ready to make a roster move with All until further medical testing. Tuesday, the Bengals moved forward after that testing, shifting All to injured reserve after confirming he suffered a torn ACL during the Week 7 win over the Baltimore Ravens. In corresponding moves, the Bengals made the signing of Cam Grandy from the Minnesota Vikings’ practice squad official. Cincinnati also placed tight end Josh Kattus on the practice squad injured list and signed Caden Prieskorn to the practice squad. So, a divvy of moves for the Bengals at tight end. With All and Tanner Hudson on injured reserve, Grandy becomes critical depth behind Drew Sample and Mike Gesicki ahead of rookie Jack Endries on the depth chart. home.headline: Cowboys vs. Eagles Injury Report
home.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. We're looking forward to this game playing on Monday night against the division rival. It's going to be a lot of fun. The atmosphere's going to be great and it's a game I wouldn't want to miss." Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So, just trying to go out there and execute. A couple guys are out. So really just, next man up. I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trust in the coaches and the game plan." Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) took a step forward and was a full participant at practice on Saturday after being limited previously in the week. The running back is listed as questionable for Monday night. Meanwhile, Jonathan Greenard (ankle), who did not practice again on Saturday, is listed as questionable. The edge rusher said it will be a game-time decision as he will need to see how his ankle feels. Alongside Greenard, the outside linebacker room is banged up. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) could return on Monday as he is listed as questionable after practicing in a limited capacity all week. Nolan Smith (concussion) has been officially ruled out. Smith is joined by defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett, tight end Grant Calcaterra, guard Landon Dickerson, and tight end Eli Stowers all participated fully in practice on Saturday. They are all listed as questionable since they are on Injured Reserve and would need to be activated by Monday afternoon in order to play against the Cowboys. home.headline: Cowboys-Eagles final injury update has 7 ruled out including Smith
home.blurb: Running back Saquon Barkley is on track to appear for the first time since leaving the Week 4 game early, and should bring a huge boost to a running game that has floundered the last three weeks. Hopefully ready to meet him in the hole is linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who hasn't seen action since Week 1 for the Cowboys. The Cowboys also expect CB Cobie Durant to return to action, and he hasn't played since Week 2. Those are two big additions for Dallas. Things are trending right for several other Cowboys, though they aren't quite ready to return to action. The Cowboys opened the 21-day practice window for LB Marist Liufau and safety PJ Locke. Both were expected to be key reserves this year and still could be activated before Monday's game, with corresponding roster moves. Starting safety Jalen Thompson can have his window opened next week. Meanwhile, Dallas did rule out WR/KR Kavontae Turpin (ribs) and LB Dee Winters (calf), along with OT Drew Shelton. McKee won't have his top two receivers as both DeVonta Smith and Dontarin Wycks have been ruled out. Barkley is one of seven listed as questionable, along with OF Landon Dickerson and edge rusher Jonathan Greenard, who is expected to be a game-time decision . Entering their Week 7 Monday Night Football matchup, the teams sport identical 2-4 records after six games , with injuries the underlying factor of both club's malaise. Dallas, implementing a new defense under first-year coordinator Christian Parker, has seen their back-seven progressively decimated week by week, undermining his attempt to get his footing as a scheme designer and playcaller. The Eagles have just lost body after body throughout their roster, losing key contributors to the offense. Are the clubs trending in opposite directions despite losing streaks for both ? Injury wise, Dallas is starting to get some contributors back, with the question being about whether they can actually make a difference or is Parker's scheme a bad one. The Eagles are trending down, still, though they will get a big boost from one returning member. For Philly, the injury discussion has centered around QB Jalen Hurts and the controversy over his blood clot diagnosis . Regardless of the inner workings there, he's been moved to IR and is done for the year, opening the door for Tanner McKee to get the start and raising the possibility if he flounders, the Eagles could turn to Joe Milton III at QB. Philly snatched him off of Dallas' practice squad last week . Here's a look at the complete injury report from Saturday.

Barkley has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury, so his return would be massive. Update: NFL insider Mike Garafolo reported that Barkley will return to practice this week and is expected to play against the Cowboys. Hunt missed Week 6 after suffering a knee and ankle injury in Week 5. He may be able to return for the Cowboys game, but he could still miss another week or two. Dickerson is on IR with a knee injury and hasn't played since Week 1. Last week, his 21-day practice window opened for the first time, and he could potentially return for the Cowboys game to start at left guard again. The Eagles have run for just 57 yards in the last two games without Barkley. This season, he averages 5.1 yards per carry, showing the Eagles' offense runs the ball better with him on the field. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. Pick: Packers 31, Panthers 24 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. picks.blurb: Vikings vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Colts WR Josh Downs reportedly wants out amid fire sale TRENDING Rays rally, avoid sweep Jayson Tatum buzzer-beater NFL Power Rankings WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Anthony Edwards injury Vikings vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 8 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Tue, October 27, 2026 at 2:38 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads As the Minnesota Vikings plan their next massive blitz, the Detroit Lions ride the wave of a big division win. These teams meet in Week 8, and here are bold predictions for the NFC North clash. It's a critical game for the Lions. The NFC North could end up with only two playoff teams. That's because the 49ers, Seahawks, and Rams still seem like firm bets. And that leaves only one other Wild Card spot. The Lions stand at 4-2 while the Vikings are 6-0. A loss would leave the Lions three games back of first place with nearly half the season in the rearview mirror. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs will rush for 100-plus yards It's tough to throw against the Vikings. They rank No. 2 in the NFL against the pass, allowing just 155 yards per game. And while their run defense is good, it's still the better path to consistently moving the football. Gibbs is fourth in the NFL with 620 yards through six games. Look for the Lions to put a saddle on him against the Vikings. Yes, the Lions are clearly overusing Gibbs already. He's almost on a record pace , according to NBC Sports. "If Gibbs keeps to his current pace of 27.7 touches per game for the entire 17-game season, he'll finish this season with a whopping 470 touches," Michael David Smith wrote. "That would be the second-most in a season in NFL history, second only to former James Wilder, who had 492 touches with the 1984 Buccaneers." Gibbs should get close to that number of touches on the ground alone. He had 29 carries against the Saints and Packers this season. Look for the neighborhood of 25 against the Vikings. He's averaging 4.6 per carry, so that easily puts him over 100. And don't worry about the injury scare late against the Packers, according to mlive.com. During his postgame media session, Lions coach Dan Campbell confirmed that Gibbs is OK and avoided serious injury . "Yeah, we got him checked," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said. "He should be good. That's that whole, 'Is it really worth going down and try to finish the game, or you just go score?' Sometimes I question that. I don't know, maybe we shouldn't just, but all good. It's a good win." Lions will double the Vikings' season average in points allowed For the season, the Vikings are allowing just 12.3 points per game. Over the last three games, they are giving up just 33 points. But the Lions will hit them for 24-plus points. Not only will Gibbs cut loose, but his runs will set up play-action daggers for Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. This is no timid prediction. The Vikings defense is the real deal. The players will even tell you that , according to The Athletic. "It's a generational group," cornerback Isaiah Rodgers said. "We've got guys who go out and trust the scheme. They trust (Flores and his staff). The stats speak for themselves." Defensive tackle Levi Drake Rodriguez said it is togetherness that brings the good outcomes. "Hopefully, that showed the joy we have on the field with each other," Rodriguez said. "We want to work hard for each other. We want to be right." But the Lions are a different beast. They are king of the offensive jungle for a reason. They rank No. 2 in the NFL with 397.3 yards per game. The NFL used to be a league where great defense would pretty much always shut down a great offense. But the rules have changed. And the Lions will cut loose for a point total the Vikings haven't allowed since 22 in the season opener against the Packers. Vikings QB Kyler Murray will have his best game of the season For all the Lions are on offense, they ain't that on defense. They rank dead last in the league with 391 yards allowed per game. Murray hasn't thrown for 250 yards in a game yet this season. In fact, he hasn't done it since 2024. And he only has three touchdown passes in basically four games played. He missed almost all of the season opener after a first-quarter injury. But the Lions are relatively decent against the run. They are an open gate against the pass. And Murray will take advantage with some chunk plays down the field. Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell is standing behind Murray, according to The Athletic. "I think our guys are very confident that we're not far off," O'Connell said. "The far-off changes a little bit as you go, but I'm very, very confident we'll get it going." One reason for optimism is that Murray has gotten better at play action. The Vikings used play action on nearly half of Murray's dropbacks in Week 7. And Murray hit on eight of 11 passes. There's still hope for Murray. Some people have been writing him off and saying the Vikings should move on, but this is a chance for him to silence critics. picks.headline: Eleventh hour NFL bold predictions for the Vikings, Broncos and Lions in Week 7
picks.blurb: Eleventh hour NFL bold predictions for the Vikings, Broncos and Lions in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Colts WR Josh Downs reportedly wants out amid fire sale TRENDING Rays rally, avoid sweep Jayson Tatum buzzer-beater NFL Power Rankings WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Anthony Edwards injury Eleventh hour NFL bold predictions for the Vikings, Broncos and Lions in Week 7 Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Oliver Fox Sun, October 25, 2026 at 3:22 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Everything in life always comes in a six-pack or a four-pack -beers, yogurt, sticks of butter, value packs of Pokemon cards . Why do we allow the numbers six and four to dominate our lives like this? On this NFL Sunday morning, I'm here to resist with a three-pack of bold predictions as we careen violently toward kickoff. The streets are saying I just didn't have time to make a six-pack, to which I will tell the streets to shut up because they're literally just made of concrete while I am a luminous being, not this crude matter. The NFC North will feature heavily, and I have more words for Bo Nix; should be a three-packtacular time! The Vikings will blow it against the Colts to lose undefeated streak Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray and wide receiver Justin Jefferson | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect But hey, this is bold predictions, not "pick a touchdown favorite to win" predictions, and the ultimate zag here would be to say that the Colts, who have launched an exploratory committee on trading their entire team , shock everyone by inverting the vibes completely. There isn't a great argument for this to happen, otherwise it wouldn't be bold, but there is an argument. The Vikings offense really is terrible; they are 27th in EPA per play ahead of absolute titans like the ... Tennessee Titans, the Miami Dolphins and the Los Angeles Chargers. They have had real difficulty moving the ball with Kyler Murray under center, and have gimmicked their way to wins with timely turnovers and crazy performance from an aggressive defense. I'm not saying that doesn't work (it clearly works), but there's no way it can work this consistently. The Colts need to stabilize behind their strengths: running the football and managing an efficient offensive attack. In Week 6 against the Titans, it felt like they held some emergency war council meeting at halftime where they all pitched their best ideas on how to best lose the game. If the team can just play to its own strengths rather than allow their weaknesses to consume them, they should have a chance. Bo Nix will be benched in the third quarter against Arizona Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect This is what we call putting the "bold" and "prediction" in bold prediction, because I could have just said something like "Bo Nix will play garbage football again and we'll all hop on our podcasts and blogs and wonder what he does," but let's get real cynical. What if the Broncos and Sean Payton lose their patience completely? Bo Nix is not a good quarterback. I don't know if he's bad, but by every metric imaginable and by the evidence of my own two eyeballs he's been remarkably ineffective this year. He can't really throw over the middle and he can't really throw deep down the sideline, so he basically just runs a college offense with a ton of handoffs, screen passes and dumpoffs with a hysterically low average depth of target. I don't think Jarrett Stidham is any better, nor am I one of those clowns constantly canvassing for unproven backups to start with no evidence that they'll be good. What I know is that the Broncos coaching staff agrees with my assessment of Bo Nix -they trust him with nothing, refuse to call any downfield shots and just try to protect, protect, protect for as long as they can while they win the game with runs, field goals and defense. If they somehow fall down big to Arizona, though? Maybe we see some emergency quarterback switch, if for no other reason than to save face with the rest of the team. Lions defense shows improvement off the bye, limits Green Bay in a big win at home Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Lions defense, so far this year, has been USDA-certified garbage. They have yet to hold a team under 20 points, get cleaved by every elite pass-catcher they encounter and had one of the most unprofessional performances I ever did see on Thursday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills in Week 2. But I, in my infinite wisdom, have decided (for some reason) that this all will get better, and it will get better right now. This is for three reasons: First, the Lions are getting Brian Branch back for the first time all year, a keystone defensive player and the kind of guy they've been missing all season. Second, they're at home, and home field still really matters in football for defensive performance -the only sport where it still really means anything. Third and finally is simple mathematical regression. No defense is in reality this unprofessional, and it's likely if not guaranteed that some of the early-season miscommunications that made the Lions defense so terrible have been ironed out. That's probably factored into the betting line, which is fascinating: Detroit is favored by 3.5 points. They're at home, and their offense is as good as it gets, but Vegas does not buy the Packers recent hot streak at all. Give me the Lions. picks.headline: Vikings at Lions: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 8 game
picks.blurb: 1. Defense wins championships, but will it win this game? The Lions and Vikings couldn't be more opposite at this point in the season. Minnesota is winning with defense, and Detroit is getting by with an electric offense. So it'll be strength vs. strength and weakness vs. weakness in this key NFC North clash. 2. Not-so smooth sailing: The Vikings are about to enter some rough waters when the calendar flips to November. Minnesota cleaned up with wins over the Saints , Dolphins and Colts in October, but the schedule's difficulty is about to be turned up a notch. The Lions, Bills, Packers and Niners await in the penultimate month of the year for the last undefeated team. We're about to find out if the Vikings are a contender or pretender. 3. Scoring drought: For the first time this season, Jahmyr Gibbs didn't get into the end zone. For someone who has his eyes on LaDainian Tomlinson's record of 31, that drought can't last much longer. Gibbs has nine total touchdowns through six games, but he'll still have to pick up the pace. That watch continues into Week 8. Lions vs Vikings odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Lions -4.5 Moneyline: Lions -218; Vikings +180 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Lions vs Vikings USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Lions 23, Vikings 20 The Vikings keep winning, and their defense keeps making everybody miserable. That travels. But the Lions present a much tougher offensive assignment than the Colts, especially with Jahmyr Gibbs creating problems as both a runner and receiver. Detroit's best approach is keeping Jared Goff out of obvious passing situations, where Brian Flores can turn an ordinary Sunday into an escape room. Minnesota's historically bad offense remains the concern. Can it consistently hold up its end against a team capable of sustaining drives? I'm expecting a tight, physical division game, with the Lions bouncing back to produce just enough offense to hand the Vikings their first loss. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Lions 20, Vikings 13 This might be the end of the line for the Vikings' undefeated run. While Brian Flores' vise-grip defense gives Minnesota a chance in any contest, it will be exceedingly difficult if the Kyler Murray-led offense remains out of sync. Deroit's defense isn't inspiring fear in anyone, but Brian Branch's return has helped the unit at least approach reliability. Jared Goff has the third-highest passer rating of any quarterback against the blitz this year, so Flores might have to be particularly creative in how he tries to box in the Lions' attack. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Lions 21, Vikings 17 Unstoppable force meets immovable object. The Lions defense couldn't catch a cold this season, and the Vikings offense appears to be doing their best to boost Brian Flores' chances of landing a head coaching job this offseason. If you like chaos, this Flores defense is for you. Physical and blitz-heavy, Minnesota is the last unbeaten team solely because of that unit. However, it's hard to have any faith in the Kyler Murray-led unit on the other side of the ball. This figures to be an ugly NFC North contest. Trust the Lions' offense to eke out a win at home. away.headline: Vikings get positive injury update on RB Aaron Jones: report
away.blurb: The veteran ball carrier exited the game in the fourth quarter as the Vikings posted 10 unanswered points to secure a 16-10 win over the visiting Colts. He was listed as questionable to return, but did not. Minnesota Vikings running back Aaron Jones left Sunday’s win over the Indianapolis Colts with a knee injury. Fortunately for the Vikings, this injury for Jones doesn’t appear to be serious. On Monday, ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported a positive update on the Vikings RB. “Vikings RB Aaron Jones’ knee injury that he suffered during Sunday’s win over the Colts is not considered to be significant at this time, and a source described him as ‘day to day,'” Schefter reported. This injury for Jones occurred in the same game that fellow running back Jordan Mason returned from injured reserve. Mason missed each of the Vikings’ last four games after suffering a thumb injury in Week 1, forcing Jones to step up as the team’s bell-cow lead back. Mason led the Vikings in rushing on Sunday, taking 15 carries for 68 yards. Jones recording 26 yards on eight carries before exiting the game. The Vikings are the NFL’s last remaining undefeated team, boasting a 6-0 recording heading into this coming Sunday’s Week 8 matchup against the Detroit Lions.
