away.headline: Detroit Lions sign former Vikings DL to practice squad, release WR
away.blurb: Originally an undrafted free agent by the Vikings in 2024 out of Oregon , Taimani finished with 22 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, one quarterback hurry, and one fumble recovery during the 2023 college football season with the Ducks. As Sunday's NFC North showdown approaches, the Detroit Lions (4-2) signed former Minnesota Vikings (6-0) defensive lineman Taki Taimani to their practice squad on Tuesday. Taimani, a 6-foot-1, 309-pound lineman, has appeared in nine NFL games (all with the Vikings ) and has registered four tackles. Per Pro Football Focus , Taimani logged 70 defensive snaps in 2024 and carded a 61.2 overall defensive grade that season. In 2025, Taimani tallied just 35 defensive snaps and had an overall defensive grade of 27.4 last season from PFF . In its corresponding move, the Lions released wide receiver Lawrence Keys from their practice squad. Detroit signed Keys back in June after a stint in the UFL with the Houston Gamblers. The 5-foot-11, 170-pound receiver finished second in the UFL with 1,001 all-purpose yards over the Gamblers' 10-game schedule. Keys registered 349 receiving yards on 24 receptions including two touchdown catches. The 26-year-old also returned 19 kickoffs for 518 yards and 11 punts for 134 yards and a 12.2 average, which ranked third in the league. After going undrafted in 2024, Keys signed with the Buffalo Bills . But, he was released prior to the start of the 2024 NFL season. During his college career at Notre Dame and then Tulane, Keys caught 81 passes for 1,080 yards and nine touchdowns. Keys' most productive collegiate season was 2023 when he hauled in 30 passes for 296 yards and two scores. Keys was waived by the Lions in August during training camp with an injury settlement before signing back onto the practice squad in late September. Head coach Dan Campbell said that it will cause the star receiver to miss practice on Wednesday before their Week 8 game against the Minnesota Vikings. Campbell added that he anticipates St. Brown returning on Thursday, but his status is unknown right now. He noted that St. Brown, along with Ennis Rakestraw, are still expected to play this week, but he was not definitive. "I think, like, he and Ennis, I think those guys will probably sit Wednesday," said Campbell. but the plan is to get them going Thursday, and I think they'll be fine; they should be good. Now, we will see when we get there." Detroit Lions Wide Receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown Has Ankle Injury Before Week 8 St. Brown played 53 snaps in the Lions' Week 7 win. It amounted to 77.9% of the snaps. That is the second-lowest rate of the season. He played 48 snaps, amounting to 74% of the snaps earlier in the year. St. Brown had a good start to his 2026 season, but it was not quite on par with other seasons, or the progression he was hoping to show. The All-Pro receiver noted that he was playing decent prior to the Packers game. "Five games into the year, I feel like I've been playing decent ball," St. Brown said when asked to describe his play. He responded with his best game of the season. St. Brown produced nine receptions for 153 yards in the Lions win. He produced nine catches for 142 yards against the Buffalo Bills in Week 2, but that was in a loss. The big impact in a winning performance made it a clear-cut best game of his season. Lions Have Crucial Stretch Upcoming The team is going to need St. Brown down the stretch run. With their first division game in Week 7, they have five more division games over the next 10 weeks.

home.blurb: C Cade Mays (Wrist, PUP) — Will return to the active roster this week S Brian Branch (Achilles, PUP) — Will return to the active roster this week On Monday, coach Dan Campbell told the media that the plan was to activate both Mays and Branch to the 53-man roster this week, but it was unclear how much either could play against the Packers. Branch is expected to “handle quite a bit,” but he may not be able to play the entire game, while Mays is expected to start based on Campbell’s comments on Wednesday : “We really worked the heck out of Cade yesterday. He got some quality reps, and we would like to give him a go here.” RB Isiah Pacheco (MCL/Back, IR) — expected to be out until December S Kerby Joseph (Knee, PUP) — expected to return to play this season Branch’s safety running mate, Kerby Joseph, also got some positive news this week, as Campbell noted on Tuesday that he still expects the All-Pro safety to return to play this season. While there is still no timetable for his return, this was the first positive update we have gotten from coaches surrounding Joseph’s status and was quickly followed up by even more promising videos posted on Joseph’s social media accounts . Ya-Sin was injured on special teams in Week 4, missed the Lions game in Week 5, but was able to get healthy enough to practice over the bye and was back on the practice field on Tuesday. While he’s no longer in the starting lineup on defense, he’s been a steady contributor on multiple phases of special teams and would boost multiple spots if he could return to game action. Wonnum also managed to play in Week 5 (50% of defensive snaps), but it’s unclear if his snaps were scaled back a tick due to injury or schematic approach. picks.blurb: 1. Klint Kubiak vowed there was "no controversy" at quarterback, where Kirk Cousins will remain the starter. While the 38-year-old might have hit a wall last week in trying to navigate the Rams ' relentless blitzes, the NFL's leading passer is hardly the Silver and Black's biggest problem. Kubiak has bemoaned an inert running game that has left Las Vegas needing to sling its way back into games. It could be tricky to get things going against a Jets defense that ranks fifth in defensive EPA per rush. 2. Can New York finally get Garrett Wilson involved early and often in the offensive game plan? One week after he was essentially a non-factor against the Patriots, Wilson was held without a reception or target in the first half against a woefully undermanned Dolphins secondary. Wilson and Glenn both downplayed the wideout's heated confrontation with quarterback Geno Smith, but expect feeding the receiver early and often to be a point of emphasis for Gang Green. 3. How the Raiders' defense handles the Jets' ground game could determine the course of the game. The Silver and Black allowed a season-high 199 rushing yards to the Rams last week, with a vulnerability that has been apparent all season finally reaching critical mass. New York, meanwhile, has seen Braelon Allen eclipse 100 rushing yards in two of the last three games he's handled as Breece Hall's fill-in. Geno Smith gets his former team, while Kirk Cousins keeps the Raiders' starting job despite the growing curiosity about Fernando Mendoza. Neither team has earned much trust lately, so let's acknowledge that before pretending this is an easy handicap. Smith threw three touchdowns against Miami, and Las Vegas' defense offers an opportunity for another productive afternoon. The Raiders need more from their running game to keep Cousins from carrying every possession. I'm giving New York the slightest edge at the Meadowlands, and a fifth straight loss for Las Vegas. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Jets 24, Raiders 20 This game could end up shaping the second half of the season for two coaching staffs that seem to be at a crossroads. The Jets' secondary might not be able to mug the Raiders' receiving corps the way that the Patriots and Rams did, but the pass rush should be able to generate sufficient heat to keep Kirk Cousins out of sorts. Las Vegas seems desperate to find any semblance of offensive balance - as well as some stops against the run - but a breakthrough might not materialize this week. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Raiders 26, Jets 20 You can put a bow on the 2026 Jets. The season, and maybe the Aaron Glenn era, came to an end with a loss to the Dolphins in Week 7. It's going to be a bumpy ride to the finish, but there is no doubt the destination is a top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That's why it's fitting that New York will get a glimpse at what it could've had last season. Fernando Mendoza won't play, but it's the idea he's wearing silver and black that sticks. The Raiders are just better. Vegas gets back on track. At home against the previously winless Miami Dolphins , the Jets' defense couldn't get off the field in the first half and didn't get the stops it needed to in a 28-25 upset loss . The boo birds were out in full force at MetLife Stadium for the Jets, who trailed 21-7 at halftime against a Dolphins' team who had yet to have a lead in a game this entire season. The saving grace? The Jets' three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft are all projected to be in the top-12 heading into Week 8 per Tankathon . The Colts ' (2-5) first-round selection is improving by the day with them going into sell mode ahead of the trade deadline. Indianapolis traded eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers on Tuesday. Now the Jets host another franchise on a losing streak, the Las Vegas Raiders , who are on a four-game skid following a 3-0 start. The Jets are in line to face QB Kirk Cousins as Raiders coach Klint Kubiak told the media that the 15-year veteran signal caller will continue to start instead of making the change to Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, reigning Heisman Trophy winner and national champion QB at Indiana. Ahead of the matchup, the Jets are dealing with several injuries, and the most notable is running back Breece Hall. He has been sidelined with a quadriceps/groin injury since Week 3, when he left the team's matchup against the Detroit Lions in the fourth quarter. Hall appeared on the practice field wearing his helmet and stretched with the team, which is an encouraging sign for his progress. New York Post Jets beat reporter Brian Costello reported that Hall eventually headed to the rehab area as reporters left practice, indicating he likely wouldn't participate in team drills. Still, his appearance on the field marks a step in the right direction. "Breece Hall is moving well at practice. I'd be optimistic about him playing. We'll know more tomorrow," Costello posted on X. With Hall sidelined, Braelon Allen has stepped into the Jets' starting running back role and has been productive as the primary back. Allen had 17 carries for 78 yards and two receptions for 26 yards last week against the New England Patriots . The week before, he logged 24 carries for 116 yards and a touchdown. However, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn made it clear that Hall will reclaim the starting job when he returns, though Allen will remain a focal point of the offense. "Breece is our starter, he's always been our starter, but Braelon is going to get touches," Glenn said earlier this week. Is Breece Hall finally ready to return for the New York Jets after today's update? The signs are pointing in the right direction. He was back on the practice field today for the first time since suffering a quad injury in the fourth quarter of New York's Week 3 game against the Detroit Lions . Hall was listed as a limited participant, and that is a welcome sight for a Jets offense that needs its lethal playmaker back. “Breece did head to the rehab area as we left practice. My guess is no team drills for him today. He will be listed as limited on the report, which he was.” What a limited practice really means for Breece Hall For those who may be unfamiliar, a limited designation on the practice report means Hall took part in practice but did not take his normal full reps. He was on the field, but he did not do everything he would normally do if he were fully healthy. Now, if Hall plays Sunday, that point goes out the window. He would have missed fewer than four games, and there would have been no reason to put him on IR. I hope that happens. Based on how he reportedly looked at practice via updates, I think Breece Hall suits up against Miami. Allen brings a different style than Hall. He is a bigger, more physical, bruising back who wears defenses down between the tackles. He isn't the receiver that Hall is out of the backfield, and that's fine, because he doesn't have to be. Hall gives the Jets the home-run speed and pass-game versatility. Allen gives them the hammer who can grind out tough yards and close out games. Put those two together, and New York has a backfield that can attack defenses in a lot of different ways. 2026 Steelers Preview: Week 8 vs. the Cleveland Browns
picks.blurb: Login/Register Home The 2026 NFL regular season is in full swing, and it's time to preview the Pittsburgh Steelers schedule ahead of every game this season. I'm going to revisit my offseason breakdown of every game on the Steelers schedule as a preview for the upcoming game. I'll be updating the odds and quarterbacks expected to play in the contest, and will only list my offseason prediction. My in-season prediction always comes both on the Steelers Preview podcast Thursday night, as well as on my Friday “Let's Ride” podcast. Here is the detailed breakdown of the Steelers 2026 regular season, continuing with the another AFC North game vs. the Browns in Pittsburgh. Week 8 vs. the Cleveland Browns Date: Sunday, November 1st – 1:00pm EST Betting Line: Opening Line: Steelers (-5.5) / Total: 39.5 Current Line: Steelers (-3.5) / Total: 39.5 Last Meeting: 12/28/25 – Browns 13, Steelers 6 Overall Series Record: Pittsburgh Steelers lead series 83-65-1 2026 Records: Steelers: 5-2 Projected Starting QB Matchup: Aaron Rodgers vs. Deshaun Watson Analysis: According to my predictions, the Steelers are coming off a win over the Saints in Paris, France. Is this going to be a letdown game with the team getting their bearings after an international game? The fact the Steelers are playing at home is a huge advantage. When you think back to the 2025 season, the Browns played an international game in London, and when they returned they didn't have a bye, but also didn't have a home game. They were forced to travel to Pittsburgh for a divisional game with rookie Dillon Gabriel at the helm. It didn't go well. Speaking of Browns quarterbacks, if everyone is healthy a question to ask will be who is the quarterback in Cleveland? I have Watson as the quarterback, but the Browns could move on to Shedeur Sanders at this stage of the season if things aren't going well with Watson at the helm. If I'm being honest, I see the Steelers winning this game with relative ease. I predicted the Steelers losing in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football earlier this season, and it is hard to believe the season series with the Browns will be over by Week 8. Nonetheless, even though the Steelers are coming off an international game, I just don't see how the Browns win this game. There used to be the Myles Garrett factor, a singular player capable of taking over a game, but Jared Verse simply isn't that type of player. When all is said and done, the Steelers win a big game heading into their bye week where they can rest and recover and get ready for a tough stretch post-bye with a prime time game in Cincinnati vs. the Bengals. Prediction: Steelers 34, Browns 17 Clearly things change from the offseason and schedule release to the upcoming game, but this game in Pittsburgh still feels pretty much the same as I thought in the preseason. I predicted the Steelers would lose on Thursday night in my preseason predictions, and I always felt as if this was a game the Steelers would win. The Steelers winning this game heading into the bye week would be the perfect way to cap off the first half of the season. It's early, but what are your thoughts on this upcoming game? Will it go as planned? Or will the Browns be able to sweep the season series with the Steelers? Let us know your thoughts in the comment section, and be sure to stay tuned to SCN for the latest news and notes on the Steelers as they press on throughout the 2026 regular season. Pittsburgh Steelers veteran safety DeShon Elliott was trending in the right direction at practice throughout the week. The team took the last step for Elliott to make his 2026 season debut Sunday against the New Orleans Saints . On Saturday, the Steelers announced they have activated Elliott from the reserve/injured list. He will be eligible to play Sunday against the Saints in the NFL's first-ever regular season game in Paris, France. Elliott fully practiced Wednesday and Thursday before the team flew to Europe. The Steelers then canceled their Friday practice in France. The veteran safety doesn't have a designation on the team's injury report. Barring a last-minute setback, Elliott will dress for the first time this season versus the Saints. On Wednesday, the Steelers released safety Rayshawn Jenkins. The team didn't make a corresponding move, which left open a roster spot for Elliott on Saturday. Elliott started this season on the PUP list because of a knee injury he sustained last season. Elliott hyperextended his knee, which required surgery, in Week 8 almost exactly a year ago on October 26. Steelers Activate DeShon Elliott for Week 7 The Jenkins release was a pretty strong giveaway that Elliott would play in Week 7. The Steelers moved on from the safety suddenly even though they later placed defensive tackle Sebastian Joseph-Day on injured reserve. Elliott will be the third for the game against the Saints. Elliott is likely to start the contest. He started 19 of 20 games from 2024-25 with the Steelers before his season-ending injury last year. In five games during 2025, Elliott posted 38 combined tackles. He also had one tackle for loss, three quarterback hits, one sack, two pass defenses and one interception. Elliott began his career in the AFC North with the Baltimore Ravens . He spent three seasons with the Ravens, where he became a regular starter in 2020. Since then, he's only not started on two occasions while being on the active roster. In 2022 and 2023, Elliott played for the Detroit Lions and Miami Dolphins . away.blurb: Falcons injury report: RB Brian Robinson, LB Divine Deablo ruled out vs. 49ers Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE Atlanta has several key players who are questionable for Sunday's matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. That includes the Atlanta Falcons and San Francisco 49ers, who each enter Sunday's game with availability questions for key players. Atlanta's injury report has been lengthy all week long, but it includes a few players who could be making a return in Week 7. Most notably are cornerbacks A.J. Terrell Jr. and C.J. Henderson. Their return would bolster a secondary that has been dinged up in recent weeks but was playing well at the start of the season. If Terrell, who has been on injured reserve for the last four games, and Henderson do return, that could afford a bit of flexibility in the secondary, especially with slot cornerback Billy Bowman Jr. ruled out for Sunday due to a hamstring injury he sustained late in Week 6. Bowman is one of four players ruled out against the 49ers. The others are linebacker Divine Deablo, offensive tackle Michael Jerrell and running back Brian Robinson Jr., the latter two of whom first appeared on Wednesday's injury report as limited participants with bicep and hamstring injuries, respectively. Deablo has been the key communicator for Atlanta's defense this season, but the team feels confident that rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels, who is questionable for the game with a neck injury , can step up in that area if needed. The Falcons had three players begin practicing this week after spending time on injured reserve. While those three players—wide receiver Beaux Collins, offensive lineman Cameron Williams and Terrell—are listed as questionable for the game, they would need to be added to Atlanta's active roster by 4 p.m. ET on Saturday to play on Sunday. away.blurb: The Atlanta Falcons will enter Sunday's matchup against the San Francisco 49ers with a lot of questions surrounding their roster availability, as four players have been ruled out and 10 others are listed as questionable. Robinson's absence was one of the more notable developments on Atlanta's final injury report. The running back was limited during Wednesday's practice before missing Thursday and Friday, ultimately being ruled out for Sunday's game. With Robinson unavailable, the Falcons will need additional contributions from their remaining running backs. Stefanski confirmed that Khalil Herbert, who is currently on the practice squad, will serve as the backup. Stefanski said he thought Terrell "looks better," suggesting the cornerback has made progress during the week. Terrell's potential return would provide a boost to a secondary that will be without Bowman and could have other defensive backs unavailable. Several other players remain questionable, including defensive linemen Samson Ebukam and Za'Darius Smith, defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. and defensive backs C.J. Henderson and Avieon Terrell. Their availability could influence Atlanta's defensive rotations and personnel packages. The Falcons must now wait for the final availability decisions before determining their game day personnel. Robinson's absence is confirmed, while Terrell's potential return and Daniels' status remain important storylines to monitor. Atlanta will look to overcome those personnel challenges when it hosts San Francisco on Sunday, with the outcome potentially hinting on how effectively its available players handle expanded responsibilities. home.headline: Is Bucky Irving Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Buccaneers vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7)
home.blurb: Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving was limited in practice to open this week due to an illness, but he returned to a full practice session on Friday. That could lead to an expanded role for Irving, who was targeted 15 times out of the backfield in Mayfield's three starts this season. The veteran running back has been solid in the 2026 campaign, averaging 4.7 yards per carry across six games. Since then, Irving has just six total targets. So, he should have a bigger workload as a pass catcher, especially with Egbuka out. Is Bucky Irving Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Buccaneers vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7) Skip to main content ON SI As a result, the Bucs decided to take him off the injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 7 matchup with the Carolina Panthers, a sign that he'll play his usual role in this matchup. Bucky Irving (illness) not listed on injury report for Week 7. Irving's presence is great news for a 1-5 Tampa Bay team that needs every win it can get to stay alive in the NFC South and the NFC playoff picture. The Bucs are expected to get quarterback Baker Mayfield (thumb) back in action on Sunday for the first time since Week 3. However, they'll be without star receiver Emeka Egbuka (foot, concussion) for the first time all season. Irving has 452 rushing yards, 74 receiving yards, two rushing scores and one receiving score this season. He'll look to build on that against a Carolina defense that has allowed the most yards per carry in the league in 2026. Let's take a look at my favorite prop for the Bucs running back now that he's set to play in Week 7. Best Bucky Irving Prop Bet vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7 Bucky Irving OVER 86.5 Rushing and Receiving Yards (-115) No team in the NFL is allowing more yards per carry this season than the Panthers (5.1), and they rank 24th in the league in EPA/Rush. So, this could be a big game for Irving, who has really come on in recent weeks, tallying 40 carries and four receptions over his last two games. Now, Irving has only cleared this line in three of his six games in 2026, but two of them came with Baker Mayfield at quarterback. Mayfield (thumb) is expected to start on Sunday, and he targeted Irving 15 times over the first three weeks of the season. home.blurb: The Buccaneers' official Friday injury report lists wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, right tackle Luke Goedeke, and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. as ruled out. Baker Mayfield remains questionable with a right thumb injury, although head coach Todd Bowles expects him to start against Carolina. Getting Mayfield back would significantly boost an offense that has struggled to establish consistency. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has done a respectable job given his limited NFL experience, but Mayfield's ability to recognize pressure, adjust protections, and make pre-snap decisions gives offensive coordinator Zac Robinson more flexibility. However, Tampa Bay's offense will be far from full strength on Sunday. Egbuka missed Wednesday and Thursday's practices with concussion and foot injuries before returning Friday in a limited capacity. Despite the improvement, the team ruled him out for Sunday's game. His absence removes one of Tampa Bay's primary receiving threats from an offense that has already struggled to create consistent opportunities downfield. Goedeke also returned to practice in a limited capacity Friday after missing the previous two sessions with a calf injury. He was ultimately ruled out, leaving Tampa Bay without its starting right tackle. Protecting Mayfield will be especially important if he returns against a Carolina defense looking to exploit an offensive line that has struggled this season. Defensively, Winfield will miss Sunday's game with a rib injury. The veteran safety was limited all week but couldn't return to game action. His absence adds to the challenge for a young defense that has shown encouraging signs despite Tampa Bay's 1-5 record. Carolina will also deal with injuries, particularly on its defensive front. Outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips and Thomas Incoom were ruled out after missing all three practices. Offensive tackle Monroe Freeling and linebacker Bam Martin-Scott are questionable despite participating fully throughout the week. The Buccaneers enter Sunday's game looking to rebound from a 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Mayfield's expected return gives Tampa Bay reason to be optimistic, but the absences of Egbuka, Goedeke, and Winfield will force the team to adjust on both sides of the ball. picks.blurb: Early odds and bold Parker Washington prediction for Colts vs. Jaguars in Week 8 Skip to main content News FanSided NFL Sites Even though the Jacksonville Jaguars didn't play in Week 7, they managed to gain ground in the AFC South , as every other team in the division lost. The Jags are back from their break and will have a prime opportunity to keep building their lead when they play the hapless Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. The Colts are 2-5 and currently showing no signs of getting better this season. Heck, they let everyone know that they're punting on the season when they ousted general manager Chris Ballard, who failed to replenish the Indianapolis roster and left it devoid of talent. Following the dismissal of Ballard, Indy has gone on to hold a fire sale, sending All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks in return for a 2027 third-round pick and a fifth in 2028 days before the Jaguars game. While the Nelson trade could incentivize the Jags to make a push for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner , they cannot lose sight of the task at hand, which is beating the dreaded divisional foe. And with this in mind, here are the early odds for Week 8 and a bold Parker Washington prediction. The Colts vs. the Jaguars early odds for Week 8 The game will be held at EverBank Stadium, where the Colts have lost 11 consecutive games. Not surprisingly, the Jaguars are a 7.5-point favorite with a moneyline of -395 , via DraftKings. Bet $395 on them to win $100 if they beat Indianapolis for a total payout of $495. The Colts' moneyline sits at +310. Place a wager of $100 and win $310 if they beat Jacksonville for a total payout of $410. The over/under for the game is set at 49.5 points. ** Keep in mind that odds are refreshed periodically, so they can change at any moment. You may also like: 5 Jaguars who need to step up after the bye Bold Parker Washington prediction for the Jaguars vs. the Colts One of the biggest storylines surrounding the Jaguars in the offseason was that they opted not to make a big splash in free agency because they wanted to take care of their homegrown talent. Thus far, they locked up long snapper Ross Matiscik, defensive end Travon Walker, cornerback Montaric Brown, and tight end Brenton Strange, so you could make the case that general manager James Gladstone achieved the goal. That said, Parker Washington is still waiting on an extension. A sixth-round pick in 2023, Washington showed flashed his first two seasons but was stucked behind Christian Kirk. Jacksonville paved the way for him to start when Kirk was traded to the Houston Texans. Right off the bat, Washington became a key contributor on offense, registering 58 receptions for 807 yards with five touchdowns, all career bests, last year. Washington wasted no time picking up where he left off last year, racking up 26 receptions for 416 yards with four touchdowns. The former Penn State Nittany Lion is on pace to register the first 1,000-yard season of his career and should have no trouble getting the top-market contract he's been looking for . Although the Jags reportedly offered Washington $25 million per year before Week 1 , he rejected the offer. It's possible that he's aiming for an annual average of $30 million. Based on his production, he may be able to get it, and he'll have a prime opportunity when he plays the Colts. Already, Washington posted his first 100-yard game of the season against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5. He'll get his second one in Week 8 when he registers seven receptions for a monster 140 yards with two touchdowns against Indy. away.blurb: Colts WR Josh Downs reportedly wants out amid fire sale LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Colts, they had some players upgraded and one added- linebacker CJ Allen. But starters Sauce Gardner, Tyler Warren, and Rigoberto Sanchez did not practice for a second straight day on Thursday, making their availability on Sunday increasingly doubtful. home.headline: Vega Ioane's injury could give Jaguars' D-line a sudden edge against Ravens
home.blurb: Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Ioane suffered an MCL sprain, adding that he'll miss time even though it's a short-term injury. The rookie hog molly left the loss to the Cincinnati Bengals and didn't return. It's hard to tell just how much time is a little time, but if it wasn't serious, Ioane would be week-to-week or questionable for Week 8. He's not, meaning that there's a strong chance he won't suit up against Jacksonville. Following their BYE, the Jacksonville Jaguars will face the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8 . And after their AFC showdown, they'll face off against the Baltimore Ravens. While it's hard to tell if Lamar Jackson will suit up for the game — he's seemingly dealing with a high-ankle sprain — the Jags now know that they probably won't have to face rookie offensive guard Vega Ioane. The Jaguars may not have to worry about Vega Ioane when they play the Ravens The Jaguars will face Baltimore in Week 9. It will be a Thursday Night game. Given that there's a three-day gap between Sunday games and Thursday, players who don't suit up Sunday often miss the Thursday bout. That doesn't bode well for Vega Ioane's availability. A first-round pick of the Ravens in 2026, Ioane got off to a strong start to his rookie season, giving up just one sack and eight total pressures in six games. Ioane began the season at right guard but eventually moved to center. He returned to right guard when Baltimore traded for Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles. Emery Jones Jr. may be the next man up. You may also like: AFC South Week 8 power ranking: The Jags win big without playing The Jaguars' D-Line must take advantage of Vega Ioane's absence Lamar Jackson has missed three games with injuries . Tyler Huntley has filled in for him, throwing for 664 yards with four touchdowns and one interception during his absence. There hasn't been that steep a drop-off at quarterback, but without Vega Ioane, the Baltimore offensive line could have trouble protecting whoever lines up behind center. This is encouraging news for a Jacksonville defensive line that has struggled to create pressure from the interior. While the Jaguars excel at stuffing the run, they have had trouble getting after the quarterback this season, registering just 11 sacks. Sure, they've racked up pressures, but those haven't always translated into big plays, takeaways, and such. Maybe the Jags can get better production from their interior defensive line after their break. Arik Armstead has played at a high level at times but has been inconsistent. On the other hand, DaVon Hamilton won't offer much in the pass-rush department, while Ruke Orhorhoro hasn't made the leap he was expected to make when he was traded to Jacksonville. Rookie Albert Regis is also in the mix but has barely played. When you add it all up, it's easy to see why the Jaguars are being urged to trade for a defensive tackle . Maybe they will, maybe they won't, but they'll at least get a bit of a break when they play the Rave

home.blurb: Return Of The 'X-Factor': Brian Branch Makes Lions A Legit Super Bowl Contender my favs Access and manage your favorites here DISMISS Scores National Football League Add FOX Sports on Google Jaguars Get Devastating Injury Update On Left Tackle Anton Harrison Published Oct. 23, 2026 1:01 p.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Jacksonville Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison will miss the remainder of the season after tearing a ligament in his right knee. Harrison injured his knee during a win against the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London on Oct. 11. He spun on the field turf to make a block and twisted his knee when he planted his right leg. Harrison was carted to the locker room. Harrison waited until the Jaguars (4-2) returned from two weeks overseas to have arthroscopic surgery to determine the extent of the damage. The scope Wednesday revealed a torn anterior cruciate ligament. Jacksonville already placed Harrison on injured reserve. Backup Walker Little, who has started 40 games over six seasons with Jacksonville, is expected to replace Harrison in the lineup the rest of the season. The injury was discovered to be more severe than initially thought during a recent procedure. Walker Little is expected to replace Harrison as the starting left tackle. The Jacksonville Jaguars will reportedly be without left tackle Anton Harrison for the remainder of the season, per NFL Media's Ian Rapoport . Harrison, who was placed on injured reserve last week after suffering a knee injury against the Philadelphia Eagles in London, suffered a torn ACL and will be sidelined for the duration of the season. Doctors found more damage than initially believed during a procedure on Oct. 22, thus leaving the Jaguars without their top blindside protector. The team exercised the fifth-year option on Harrison in April, which ties him to the club through the 2027 season. The former first-rounder was playing his first season at left tackle in the NFL after winning the job in training camp. He stepped in for the injured Cole Van Lanen , who's 2025 season ended after a knee injury sidelined him last year. Van Lanen started training camp on the Physically Unable to Perform list, working to the side as he rehabbed for a majority of the preseason. He returned to the field as Jacksonville's right tackle, with Harrison winning the job of protecting Trevor Lawrence's back. Walker Little will fill in for Harrison for the remainder of the season as he did last week against the Houston Texans . away.blurb: These are the players who did not practice and are not on an injury list. Rookie running back Kaelon Black returned to practice after being sidelined by an adductor injury. His return is significant for a running back room that has been dealing with several training camp injuries. "They just said he has some tightness, so we were just being smart, taking him out," head coach Kyle Shanahan said after practice. "I don't think it's anything worse, so we'll see when we get in there, but nothing that I'm worried about right now." "But I thought, from the jump, K.B. came out running pretty hard, so it was exciting to see him back." "Honestly, I don't think it was our best day," Purdy said. "I feel like fundamentals and stuff were just a little off and whatnot. Obviously there was some good stuff, some stuff we need to work on, but I just feel like we could have come out with a little bit more chip on our shoulder, offensively." "Anytime you get to go against another team, it's a great opportunity to see where you stand," linebacker Fred Warner said. "I always look forward to joint practices for that reason—to come out and be in a game-like setting against another opponent. Luckily, it was a good test for us." Defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa continued to stand out with consistent pressure on Chargers quarterbacks. It's worth noting that several of the 49ers' pass-defense deficiencies during practice—had this been an actual game—likely would have been negated by Odighizuwa's sacks. away.headline: Chargers All-Star Offensive Lineman Returns to Practice, Quieting Season-Ending Rumors
away.blurb: While it has been an odd season filled with surprises, one thing has been unsurprising: injuries piling up for players in the Powder Blue uniform. Injuries always seem to happen for the Chargers, an unfortunate certainty fans can count on year in and year out. Alt has officially returned to practice today, Oct. 21, the Chargers' first practice since losing to the Chiefs. Along with his return, the Chargers' starting left guard, Kayode Awosika , has also returned to practice after missing time with his fibula injury. He missed a total of four games. Now that the Chargers are back with two more of their offensive linemen, the offensive line will once again be shuffled to ensure the "best 5" are out in front of Justin Herbert. With rookies Travis Burke, Logan Taylor and Alex Harkey all being starters over the last two weeks, who will be the rookies to be replaced first? The only step left for the Bolts is to see Rashawn Slater return from injured reserve and get this offensive line back to health. Who knows if that will be enough to turn the team around, but seeing Herbert have healthy linemen in front of him will hopefully bring more morale. Chargers All-Star Offensive Lineman Returns to Practice, Quieting Season-Ending Rumors Skip to main content SI.COM The Los Angeles Chargers have started the 2026 NFL season at 0-6, marking them as officially the worst team in the NFL. They have dealt with injuries, poor play from multiple units and extremely poor coaching from coaches who seemingly have never had a track record of being bad. One of the biggest injuries suffered thus far in the 2026 NFL season has been Pro Bowl offensive tackle, former Top 5 selection, Joe Alt. Alt suffered a neck injury against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 4 due to a freak helicopter-esque kick from Seahawks defender Nick Emmanwori. The play where Joe Alt is injured by Seahawks DB Nick Emmanwori pic.twitter.com/2P0KMGTzAl Cannot exactly say I have seen anything like that happen in an NFL game, but also I cannot say I thought the Chargers were going to be 0-6 to start this NFL season either. Moving on, Alt has missed two games: the Chargers' losses to the Denver Broncos and the Kansas City Chiefs. Anytime you are dealing with a neck injury, it is important to prioritize safety over rushing back, allowing Alt to spend time with a specialist and get clearance to begin practicing on Oct. 18. RT Joe Alt (neck) and LG Kayode Awosika (fibula) were participating during the portion of today’s Chargers practice open to the media. Who is the Starting 5 OL for the Chargers After the Bye Week? LT: Travis Burke LG: Kayode Awosika C: Jake Slaughter RG: Cole Strange RT: Joe Alt This lineup sees Harkey and Taylor being replaced by Alt and Awosika, returning from their respective injuries. Burke continues in his role as the third tackle, continuing what has been a pretty impressive season for the fourth-round rookie. Published Oct 22, 2026 NATE GOSNEY Nate Gosney is lifelong Chargers fan

Per the report, his status is "up in the air" for the Rams (2-4) for Sunday's road game against the Las Vegas Raiders (3-3). Los Angeles head coach Sean McVay is expected to speak to reporters on Friday. The Rams will be without fellow wideout Davante Adams, who was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week with a ruptured hamstring. The other members of the receiver room are Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Alex Bachman. home.headline: Rams week 7 injury report: Puka Nacua, Trent McDuffie questionable vs. Raiders

As the Rams prepare for their Week 8 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers, Garrett is nearing a potential return. While the Rams haven't established an official timeline, outside reports have consistently pointed to a six-week recovery. After missing the Rams' game against the Las Vegas Raiders, Garrett has officially missed six games and is now just over six weeks removed from knee surgery. A six-week timeline was always seen as a worst-case scenario for Garrett, and he has now reached that point. Still, McVay remained mum on Garrett's potential return to practice this week. Late last week , NFL Media's Ian Rapoport reported that Garrett was likely to return to practice this week and could play in Week 8. McVay even said on Friday that Garrett returning to practice next week was a possibility, but that he'd wait to talk to Garrett and the team's training staff to come to a decision. It's no real surprise that the Rams remain coy on Garrett's injury, as that's how they've handled it since the beginning . Garrett was initially held out of practice late in training camp due to knee swelling. While he played in Week 1, Garrett didn't feel like himself and was placed on injured reserve the following week. McVay is scheduled to speak to the media again on Wednesday. At that time, McVay may have more information about Garrett's status. If Garrett isn't practicing by Thursday, it seems unlikely that he'll return this week. When the Rams designated Keagen Trost to return from injured reserve, they opened his 21-day window on the Thursday before the game. If Garrett does return to practice and ends up playing this week, it would provide a huge boost to the defense. While the defense has played well, it has struggled to generate consistent pressure on opposing quarterbacks. The Rams rank 27th in sack rate this season. Not that anyone in Broncos Country needs a reminder. Denver was flogged 31-10 by the Kansas City Chiefs. And the Broncos defense still hasn't tackled Kenneth Walker. Thankfully, and hopefully, Denver gets a crack at a redo this Sunday in Denver. A win at home against Patrick Mahomes, Walker, and Kansas City would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West. FanDuel Sportsbook has Denver as the home underdog at +1.5 points, though that's basically a pick 'em at this point. The total sits over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Win the turnover battle As we saw in the Thursday night win over the Seattle Seahawks, when the Broncos defense creates turnovers and the offense protects the ball, Denver wins. Force Mahomes into some rushed throws and/or punch the ball out to give Bo Nix and the offense some added possessions. On top of that, Nix and the offense need to continue to protect the ball. The Broncos have won three straight, but their injury picture matters, particularly with Patrick Surtain II and Jaylen Waddle. The Chiefs have their own issues to sort through, and the Week 1 blowout doesn't tell us how this rematch will unfold. We should get a considerably tighter game, with both defenses making the offenses work. I'm not sure I trust Patrick Mahomes, given the lack of quality pass-catchers around him, but I do trust Kenneth Walker III against one of the NFL's worst run defenses on the heels of a homecoming dud. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Chiefs 17, Broncos 10 Even with all of their readily evident limitations, it's hard to believe the Chiefs could turn up truly putrid offensive performances in back-to-back weeks. Denver, on the other hand, might be dealing with its own regression to the mean, as it seems unlikely that last week's explosive plays will carry over against the Chiefs. A rout similar to Week 1 might not be in the cards, but Kansas City should be able to escape with the sweep. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Broncos 20, Chiefs 16 This should be a marquee game, but now it feels like just another game on the Sunday slate – due in part to a sleep-inducing Broncos' offense and very flawed Chiefs team. Kansas City's Week 1 blowout victory over Denver feels like a lifetime ago, and maybe that's because it was. Bo Nix showed some signs of life last week, while Patrick Mahomes is running out of receivers. If the Chiefs can't win by handing the ball off to Kenneth Walker III, they can't win. Denver knows that. We know that. The home team wins in the Mile High City. Sunday, Nov 1 · 4:25 PM ET · Empower Field at Mile High · CBS, Paramount+ Chiefs vs Broncos Betting Odds (BetUS) Kansas City Chiefs Adding Kenneth Walker III has made life much easier for Patrick Mahomes. He had a quiet day in the 20-3 loss to the Seahawks, where they were extra motivated to shut him down on his return to Seattle. Kansas City needs to bounce back after that defeat. Mahomes had one of his worst games in years, throwing for just 165 yards with no touchdowns and an interception. Bo Nix hasn’t been at his best and may struggle to push the ball downfield, but Denver’s defense is winning games. The unit has 21 sacks through seven games, and while its overall numbers don’t jump off the page, its impact is huge. Defensive end Zach Allen has 4.5 sacks, and linebacker Alex Singleton leads the NFL with 87 tackles. Chiefs vs Broncos Predictions With the total at 41.5, the under is our pick. away.headline: Chiefs Designate 2nd-Round Draft Pick to Return From PUP List
away.blurb: Chiefs Designate 2nd-Round Draft Pick to Return From PUP List They officially placed offensive tackle Josh Simmons on injured reserve, costing him at least four more games in addition to missing every game so far this season. Wide receiver Rashee Rice has been out with a hamstring injury each of the last two weeks. However, the Chiefs got a promising developmental player back on Wednesday. Kansas City Chiefs Designate DT Omarr Norman-Lott to Return From PUP List According to a report from The Kansas City Star's Sam McDowell, the Chiefs have designated second-year defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott to return from the physically unable to perform list. Unlock the latest Heavy on Chiefs news — direct to your inbox. Updated Oct 28, 2026 at 12:39pm The Kansas City Chiefs have taken a hit from numerous injuries over the past few weeks. Norman-Lott did not participate in training camp or preseason as he continued to rehab from a torn ACL he sustained in his right knee during a Week 7 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders last season. He was placed on the PUP list ahead of the start of the regular season. Norman-Lott now has a 21-day window where he can practice, then the Chiefs have to decide whether or not they are going to activate him to the 53-man roster. They will likely give him the entire window to ramp up after missing nearly a full year of action. Another reason Kansas City doesn't need to rush Norman-Lott back is because it has impressive depth at defensive tackle. Chris Jones is obviously the start of the show, and the Chiefs added free agent veteran Khyiris Tonga during the offseason. Tonga has been stout against the run, and has contributed on offense as a fullback . Kansas City also drafted Peter Woods in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Woods hasn't made a splash on the stat sheet yet, but has helped provide pressure on opposing quarterbacks while also giving the run defense a boost. Jones, Tonga, and Woods have settled in as an impactful rotating trio. The Chiefs have even given defensive end Felix Anudike-Uzomah looks at defensive tackle. Anudike-Uzomah has displayed impressive versatility this season , and is remaining healthy after an injury-riddle beginning to his career. Broncos get bad news on Jaylen Waddle after injury suffered on poorly designed play call | Sporting News Skip to main content SN 140 Horse Racing Horse Racing Latest News More Sports More Sports Latest News Fantasy Fantasy See More Football News Betting Betting See More Explore Betting Home Predictions Prediction Markets See More Explore Predictions Home Watch Watch How to Watch Streaming Services Apple TV The Denver Broncos are on a three-game winning streak right now and head into a Week 8 rematch against the Kansas City Chiefs with a real chance of making up ground in the AFC West. But there is some real concern about the offense, and it's not just about Bo Nix and Sean Payton. The issue for Denver now is all about wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, who suffered an injury in the Week 7 win over the Arizona Cardinals . According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Waddle aggravated a chest injury he already had on the reverse that was nearly disastrous. Waddle lost a lot of yards and nearly lost the ball, and now it's confirmed he got hurt on the poorly designed play. Jaylen Waddle aggravates injury on poorly designed play call "Broncos WR Jaylen Waddle, suffered an aggravation of his previous chest injury on the reverse last week and his status for Sunday vs the Chiefs will be determined at a later time, sources say," Rapoport reports. This report from Rapoport confirms that the Denver receiver is not a lock to suit up for the team in Week 8, which could prove to be a pivotal matchup for the AFC West division title this season. With Pat Bryant already on injured reserve, that would leave Courtland Sutton as the No. 1 target, with Troy Franklin and the running back trio of J.K. Dobbins, Jonah Coleman, and RJ Harvey likely to see a lot of involvement this week. MORE : Browns not expected to trade Jerry Jeudy despite plenty of speculation It's too early to tell if Waddle will play or not, but the uncertainty is enough to spark some concern. There's a real chance that Waddle, if he doesn't practice much this week, could miss Week 8's matchup. This injury occurred on a play that had Waddle running in the backfield on a reverse, which went horribly wrong and nearly led to a Denver turnover. It lost 12 yards in total, and might've made Denver lose Waddle for a week. Payton admitted afterwards it was a horrible play, but the damage was already done. Waddle's now banged up and in question for Week 8. home.headline: Broncos’ injuries have revealed the depth behind Vance Joseph’ elite defense
home.blurb: Abrams-Draine and Robinson stood out in training camp. Both have shown the potential to contribute as starters, and their presence on the two-deep is a luxury for Denver. Barron is a former first-round pick in whom the Broncos have invested in the future. Team officials have seen what Barron can do in high-pressure situations, from facing a Kyle Shanahan offense, matching up against Cardinals tight end Trey McBride and facing Jaxon Smith-Njigba, one of the NFL's most productive receivers. Those lessons cannot be replicated in practice. Robinson has followed a similar path. With Cooper out, the young edge rusher has started to come on in recent weeks. With Elliss out and Cooper back, Robinson could shift into a more limited role. But if his pass-rush production keeps trending up, Denver might struggle to keep him off the field. Robinson has posted a 14.1% pressure rate, second on the team among players with at least 100 pass-rush reps, according to Next Gen Stats. “The sky is the limit for this guy. Me and coach kind of have a running joke like you better buy some stock on him now because here in the next couple games and the rest of the season you just see the improvement game in and game out,” Key said. “I love to see it for Que. He's having a time out there and he definitely plays with a lot of emotion and you can see it.” That matters as Denver enters the stretch run. The return of Surtain, Hufanga and Cooper should make the defense stronger, but the value of their absences could extend beyond the games they missed. The Broncos now have more evidence of what their younger players can do when the stakes are real — and that knowledge could prove just as important as getting their starters back. Branded Content Advertising by Ascend 1st ski area opens for season ⛷️ Denver has weathered injuries to key defenders, giving young players like Kris Abrams-Draine and Que Robinson a chance to develop The Broncos' defense has been one of the NFL's best over the past four weeks, but the stretch has revealed something just as important: Denver's depth is in a rare class. Denver has played without three of its top defenders — Patrick Surtain II, Talanoa Hufanga and Jonathon Cooper — for stretches this season. Their absences have forced younger players and reserves into meaningful roles, giving the coaching staff a better look at what it has behind its starters. The Broncos' defense is undeniably better with Surtain, Hufanga and Cooper in the fold. They are three of the team's highest-paid players and also rank among the best at their positions in the NFL. Surtain is a multiple-time All-Pro cornerback, Hufanga was named AFC Defensive Player of the Week earlier this season and Cooper is an effective edge rusher. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph will certainly welcome the trio back with open arms. But in the stretch without those three players, the Broncos learned a lot about the depth on their roster . home.headline: Injury Report: CB Pat Surtain II and RB Jonah Coleman questionable for Week 7 vs. Cardinals, 3 Broncos ruled out
home.blurb: Injury Report: CB Pat Surtain II and RB Jonah Coleman questionable for Week 7 vs. Cardinals, 3 Broncos ruled out Skip to main content Primary nav Game Day ENGLEWOOD, Colo. — A pair of Broncos could return for Denver's Week 7 matchup against the Cardinals. Cornerback Pat Surtain II (ankle) and running back Jonah Coleman (ankle) were listed as questionable for Sunday's matchup in Arizona on the team's final injury report of the week. Surtain, who has not played since Week 4 against the 49ers, remained a limited participant for the third consecutive practice. The All-Pro cornerback returned to practice this week after missing Denver's wins over the Chargers and Seahawks. While Surtain and Coleman were listed as questionable, running back Tyler Badie (thumb), outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) were ruled out. All three players did not practice during the week ahead of Sunday's game. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) improved to a full participant on Friday after being limited in Denver's first two practices of the week. Waddle was not assigned a game status, which indicates he will be available to play on Sunday. Defensive lineman Zach Allen (not injury related – rest) and cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) were also full participants on Friday and not assigned game statuses. Running back Jonah Coleman provides "juice" in his return to game action. Running back Jonah Coleman is active and officially available for Week 7 after being activated from injured reserve on Saturday. Coleman was a full participant for the third consecutive day, and he would be eligible to play against the Cardinals if he is activated from injured reserve. Coleman, who was placed on injured reserve following Week 2, began his 21-day practice window on Wednesday. picks.headline: Patriots opponent preview: Are the Dolphins trending up?

Bernd Buchmasser Wed, October 28, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Coming off their mini-bye, the New England Patriots return to their division. On Sunday, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel will visit the Dolphins in Miami. The Dolphins are in the middle of a rebuild. They brought in Jeff Hafley and Malik Willis as the head coach-quarterback combo this offseason to replace the departed Mike McDaniel and Tua Tagovailoa, and have invested heavily in rookie talent: no team made more picks in this year's draft than Miami's 13. The organization is building for the future, even though there are some current growing pains. At 1-5 and ranked 30th in scoring differential thus far, the Dolphins have been one of the worst teams in the NFL this season up to that point. That said, they might be trending up. Let's meet them. Dolphins key stats The Dolphins' problems are reflected by their statistics. They are ranked near the bottom of the league in most major categories on both offense and defense. 1-5 (4th AFCE) 4-3 (2nd AFCE) Scoring diff. Points allowed/game Off. yards/game Off. EPA/play -0.122 (29th) Off. EPA/dropback -0.116 (28th) -0.130 (20th) -0.200 (26th) Def. yards/game Def. EPA/play Def. EPA/dropback -0.115 (13th) -0.081 (22nd) Turnover diff. Offensively, the Dolphins have struggled moving the ball both through the air and on the ground. There have been flashes, but the consistency is lacking even though the team has been able to keep turnovers in a comparatively reasonable range (especially when looking to New England's much more talented offense). On defense, a lack of takeaway has plagued the unit, as has an uneven pass rush and an inability to get off the field on third down (52.1%; 31st). The run defense has been a relative bright spot, but considering that opponents are throwing all over the Dolphins — fourth-most attempts (175), highest net yards per attempt (7.5), highest scoring percentage (49.1%) — there simply is no need to run into a veteran D-line on a regular basis. Dolphins 2026 season The Dolphins started their season with five straight losses, including the first three by multiple scores. Since then, however, they have shown some improvement. Their scoring margin of -7 over the last three games is a distinct improvement, as is being able to finally earn a victory last Sunday against the lackluster Jets. Week 1: 27-13 loss at Las Vegas Raiders (0-1) Week 2: 35-13 loss at San Francisco 49ers (0-2) Week 3: 24-10 loss vs. Kansas City Chiefs (0-3) Week 4: 15-10 loss at Minnesota Vikings (0-4) Week 5: 31-24 loss vs. Cincinnati Bengals (0-5) Week 6: Bye Week 7: 28-25 win at New York Jets (1-5) What stands out about Miami's schedule is that it featured the last three unbeaten teams in the league — the 49ers, Chiefs and Vikings — and the toughest strength of schedule among all 32 teams (.667). Granted, the Dolphins being fairly bad played into that, but they have played, and lost to, some very good teams and beaten the worst one they have faced so far. Dolphins active roster Roster up-to-date as of Oct. 28, 5 a.m. ET | *denotes nominal starter Quarterback (2): Malik Willis* (2), Kyle McCord (14) Running back (3): Ollie Gordon II* (0), Jaylen Wright (5 | KR), Kaytron Allen (30) Fullback (1): D.J. Herman (34) Wide receiver (6): Malik Washington* (6 | PR), Chris Bell* (18), Caleb Douglas* (7), Kevin Coleman Jr. (21), Jared Wayne (86), Jalen Tolbert (1) Tight end (4): Greg Dulcich* (85), Will Kacmarek (89), Seydou Traore (83), Justin Joly (80) Offensive tackle (4): Patrick Paul* (52 | LT), Austin Jackson* (73 | RT), Caedan Wallace (77), Chukwuebuka Godrick (79) Interior offensive line (6): Kadyn Proctor* (74 | LG), Aaron Brewer* (55 | C), Jonah Savaiinaea* (71 | RG), Jarrett Kingston (62), Andrew Meyer (60), D.J. Campbell (63) Interior defensive line (4): Zach Sieler* (92), Jordan Phillips* (94), Kenneth Grant (78), Zeek Biggers (93) Defensive edge (5): Joshua Uche* (9), Chop Robinson* (44), Malik Herring (90), Rob Beal Jr. (51), Rodney McGraw (59) Linebacker (5): Jacob Rodriguez* (10), Jordyn Brooks* (20), Willie Gay Jr. (40), Jackson Woodard (42), Shaka Heyward (45) Cornerback (6): Chris Johnson* (3), Jason Marshall Jr.* (4), JuJu Brents* (8), Jaylin Simpson (32), Reese Taylor (35), Marcellas Dial Jr. (24) Safety (5): Michael Taaffe* (16), Dante Trader Jr.* (11), Zayne Anderson (23), Julius Wood (25), Kyle Louis (19) Specialists (2): Bradley Pinion (48 | P/H), LS Tucker Addington (46 | LS) The first thing that stands out about the Dolphins is their commitment to rebuilding from the ground up. As part of that process, they have six rookie starters in their lineup: wide receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas and left guard Kadyn Proctor on offense, plus linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, cornerback Chris Johnson and safety Michael Taaffe on defense. Furthermore, several of their key reserves are first-year players as well, including fullback D.J. Herman, WR4 Kevin Coleman Jr, and their entire three-man backup tight end group. How soon the Dolphins will add a quarterback to the mix will be seen. For now, however, they are riding with free agency signing Malik Willis. Willis has started all six of the team's games since signing a three-year, $67.5 million contract to move from Green Bay to Miami alongside his head coach. In those games, he has completed 87 o f 151 pass attempts (57.6%) for 1,057 yards with four touchdowns and interceptions each. He also has been sacked 16 times and scored three rushing touchdowns. Willis is a hit-or-miss thrower with big-play potential, but overall has been uneven as evidenced by his 31st ranking among quarterbacks in EPA per play (-0.115). Part of the reason might be his supporting cast, which is missing its best player — running back De'Von Achane — and relying on a whole lot of young talent. That said, Willis' top two receivers this year are both veterans: wide receiver Malik Washington (26/289/0) and tight end Greg Dulcich (18/213/0). At running back, meanwhile, Ollie Gordon has stepped up since Achane's season-ending knee injury. He has carried the. ball 72 times for 339 yards and a 4.7-yard average per carry; Gordon also has scored a team-leading four times. Miami's offensive line, meanwhile, is a collection of highly-drafted players. The only non-first- or second-round pick is center Aaron Brewer, a former undrafted free agent who started his career with Mike Vrabel's Titans in 2020. On the other side of the ball, Miami is led by a veteran defensive line. The top players among the group are Zach Sieler and Chop Robinson, who are tied for the team lead with two sacks each. Robinson, meanwhile, has posted a team-high 20 quarterback pressures. Also high on both lists is ex-Patriot and started edge Joshua Uche, who has one quarterback takedown among his 13 pressures. The second level of the defense is led by the aforementioned Jacob Rodriguez, who has impressed since arriving in the second round of this year's draft. His running mate off the ball is first-team All-Pro Jordyn Brooks, who signed a three-year, $48.1 million extension through 2029 this offseason. The Dolphins are banking on Rodriguez and Brooks leading their defense for years to come, and for good reason: both are very good players. The secondary doesn't have the same consistent talent, even though it has received some solid contributions from its youngsters and veterans alike. Safety Michael Taaffe, for example, is leading the team with two interceptions and tied for the team lead with a forced fumble. Overall, however, as illustrated by the EPA per dropback ranking, the Dolphins' pass defense has some ground to make up — and an inconsistent secondary is a big reason for that. Interestingly enough, the Dolphins don't have a kicker on their active roster. Riley Patterson was released after missing three kicks over the first five games, with the team relying on practice squad member Zane Gonzalez since. In his lone game, Gonzalez has not attempted any field goals but gone a perfect 4-for-4 on extra points. Dolphins reserves Practice squad (16): QB Brady Cook (15), RB Carlos Washington Jr. (26), WR A.J. Henning (82), WR Jalen Reagor (88), WR Will Sheppard (81), TE Tre Watson (87), OT Gottlieb Ayedze (72), OL James Easter (65), DT Jordan Jefferson (91), ED Amari Gainer (53), ED Max Llewellyn (57), ED Eric Watts (95), LB Liam Anderson (50), CB Ethan Bonner (27), S Major Burns (43), K Zane Gonzalez (31) IR (6): RB De'Von Achane (28), TE Cole Turner (87), DT Rene Konga (95), LB Ronnie Harrison (56), LB Trey Moore (17) PUP (1): CB Darrell Baker Jr. (22) The most prominent name on the Dolphins' reserve lists is without a doubt De'Von Achane, who will miss the remainder of the season with a torn ACL suffered in Week 3. Coming off a season in which he had 1,838 scrimmage yards and 12 touchdowns, a healthy Achane would be Miami's lead running back and most dangerous offensive player. Dolphins coaching staff Head coach: Jeff Hafley Coordinators: Bobby Slowik (OC), Sean Duggan (DC), Chris Tabor (ST) The Dolphin overhauled their coaching staff this offseason, firing Mike McDaniel and brining in Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley. Patriots might know Hafley from another role, though: he was Boston College's head coach between 2020 and 2023. Hafley brought coordinator Sean Duggan and a significant portion of the defensive staff with him, and also hired Chris Tabor to lead the special teams unit. On offense, there is a bit more continuity: coordinator Bobby Slowik already was with the Dolphins under McDaniel, previously serving as a senior passing game coordinator.

away.headline: Callahan: The Patriots just finished self-scouting. This is the what they saw
away.blurb: First, they took a long weekend. Then, eight starters sat out Monday’s practice, presumably a day of veteran rest , and players were off again Tuesday. As for the coaches, Mike Vrabel and staff split their time between preparing for Miami and self-scouting, a process that doesn’t require nearly the time as it used to. Because when reporters and paying fans have access to thousands upon thousands of metrics and all-22 film on every player and team, coaches no longer need extra days to sort out their own mess. Smart teams, like the Pats, do this every week, updating themselves on their own tendencies while they study their opponents’. Plus, anyone who watched the Patriots miss 17 tackles in Chicago could have told you what Kevin Byard did Monday when asked what the most important piece of intel was on the defense’s self-scouting report. The gap between their success in man and zone coverage is not tenable for a contender, no matter how much man-to-man the Patriots want to play and especially considering certain teams have been able to spook them out of playing it before kickoff (Jacksonville and Buffalo). The good news is, there are reasons to believe this gap will close because coverage choice and success are directly tied to other factors that should change soon. Bears quarterback Caleb Williams and Jets quarterback Geno Smith went a combined 8-for-8 for 127 yards and two touchdowns on play-action passes against base personnel, a slower grouping where the Patriots are least likely to play their preferred man-to-man. Those plays hurt the Pats’ overall zone numbers, which can be ameliorated if they better stop the run out of nickel personnel in the first place. The Patriots’ best run-blocker, right guard Mike Onwenu, is out for the year. Their starting left guard just landed on injured reserve. Their new fullback is on IR, and has an injury he’s been managing since last season. Since they returned from Chicago last week, the Patriots have been busy. More like, in-season self-care. “We pride ourselves on being a really good tackling secondary,” Byard told reporters. “We haven’t been doing that the past couple games, so that’s something we definitely have to improve on.” How to maximize self-care — sorry, self-scouting — is less obvious now in an era of abundant information. There are at least two non-negotiable steps: No. 1: Separate the metrics that matter and weigh them accordingly. No. 2: Decide what to fix and how. Vrabel spoke to this during a Monday morning interview on WEEI. “Some things that we can reasonably improve on, and some things we’re just going to have to be OK that we’re probably not going to be able to improve on,” he said. Considering they ranked among the NFL’s better tackling defenses last year and carried over most of the same roster, tackling ought to be fixable. Just drill it Herb Brooks-style: again. Again. away.blurb: Another option is Roy Lopez of the Arizona Cardinals. He has the 12th-best PFF run defense grade among defensive tackles (minimum 80-plus run snaps) this season. If the Buccaneers are willing to sell, could A'Shawn Robinson be available? He has Pro Football Focus' second-highest run defense grade for defensive tackles. The Bucs are 2-5, but the NFC South leaders are 3-3, so Tampa Bay could still make a run for the division title. Starting right guard Mike Onwenu is on IR due to a fractured ankle. Starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker missed Week 7 with a hamstring injury and it's unknown when he'll return. He's also on IR. Vera-Tucker has missed a ton of games due to injuries throughout his career, so his availability is not guaranteed. The top guard available on the trade market -- Colts eight-time Pro Bowler Quenton Nelson -- was dealt to the Seattle Seahawks on Tuesday . Other potential targets at guard include Andrew Wylie of the Washington Commanders, Jackson Powers-Johnson of the Las Vegas Raiders and Ben Bredeson of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Wylie can play tackle or guard. The Chargers are a disaster with an 0-6 record. Could veteran edge rusher Khalil Mack be available for the right price? Mack isn't a dominant player at this stage of his career, but he's still a good pass rusher. He has three sacks and 16 pressures in six games for the Chargers. Colts wideout Josh Downs could be available. Downs is a good route runner against man coverage and has a history with Drake Maye. Downs and Maye enjoyed two productive seasons together at the University of North Carolina in 2022 and 2023. picks.blurb: 1. Philadelphia needs a reset: The Eagles have dropped five straight after a 2-0 start, with Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys moving them to 2-5. Another division loss would make an already difficult climb even steeper for a team that's more realistically already on to 2027 due to so many key injuries. 2. Keep an eye on Saquon: Speaking of injuries, Saquon Barkley played only nine snaps Monday while dealing with hamstring and back issues. He offered an encouraging assessment of his hamstring and said he doesn't expect the back problem to keep him out. His practice workload still warrants watching. 3. The preparation advantage favors Washington: The Commanders come off their bye, while the Eagles turn around from Monday night for a Sunday road game. That's valuable extra time to prepare for Tanner McKee and the Eagles' reshuffled offense. 4. McKee needs help from his defense: Philadelphia's quarterback threw for 211 yards, one touchdown and one interception against Dallas. The Eagles produced three touchdown drives, but their defense couldn't slow the Cowboys. Sustaining drives only helps so much if the other team keeps answering. 5. We should expect points: With a game total around 40.5, we're not asking for much to hit 41 points, even from these two offenses. The trends are on our side. Commanders coach Dan Quinn is 8-1 to the over in division games since the start of last season, while the Eagles are 7-1 to the over against the Commanders under coach Nick Sirianni. Commanders vs Eagles odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Eagles -1.5 Moneyline: Eagles -125; Commanders +105 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Commanders vs Eagles USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Commanders 24, Eagles 17 Philadelphia showed some offensive life Monday, but the injury situation keeps getting in the way. Saquon Barkley aggravated his hamstring and played only nine snaps, leaving another major question around an offense already operating without Jalen Hurts. Tanner McKee can keep things functional when the Eagles protect him and stay balanced. That becomes much harder if the Commanders take away the run and force longer passing situations. Washington also has the benefit of a bye and lots of extra rest, while Philadelphia turns around from Monday night. It's so disappointing this is a primetime game. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Eagles 19, Commanders 14 Seldom has prime time featured two teams facing such desperation around midseason. The severely shorthanded Eagles offense finally showed signs of life against the Cowboys, though the once-reliable defense suffered perhaps its worst performance of the Vic Fangio era. Expect a bounce-back outing against a Washington team short on weapons. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Commanders 23, Eagles 13 The Commanders haven't won a game that Jayden Daniels started in since Oct. 5, 2025. Washington is 0-7-1 in the eight starts after that victory, but the time has come as the team comes out of the bye. They have run out of alarms to describe the fire on Dan Quinn's seat, making this contest a must-win for the Commanders to have any chance of making the playoffs in a weak NFC East. Against a battered and bruised Eagles squad that is running out of players, there is no better time for Washington to get back in the win column. away.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So, just trying to go out there and execute. A couple guys are out. So really just, next man up. I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trust in the coaches and the game plan." The veteran quarterback went down in the week four loss against the Indianapolis Colts in London with what the team described as a knee injury, allowing rookie Athan Kaliakmanis to make his NFL debut after replacing him before Mariota avoided injury reserve. Omenihu has missed the last two games with a groin/ankle injury, marking a welcomed return for the defensive line's depth. Yet there was some bad news after Quinn revealed defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw remains sidelined as head coach Dan Quinn noted his recovery has not materialized as hoped. Kinlaw has battled through injuries in his second season with the franchise despite not missing any games yet, though whether he will ultimately be available in week eight remains to be seen. On the flip side, how healthy the Eagles are in week eight remains to be seen with defensive back Michael Carter, wide receiver DeVonta Smith, outside linebacker Nolan Smith and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks all ruled out for the Monday night matchup against the Dallas Cowboys in week seven. That doesn't include running back Saquon Barkley among the over dozen of Eagles who drew the questionable tag in the latest injury report, while head coach Nick Sirianni is still battling through the sudden retirement of All-Pro offensive tackle Lane Johnson. Quarterback Tanner McKee is also set to start in week seven with Jalen Hurts sidelined for the remainder of the season. These two teams are both in second place in their respective divisions, and this game could have massive wild card implications in the NFC. Caleb Williams gets a demanding follow-up assignment after leading Chicago past New England in a high-scoring game last Thursday. 2. Watch Seattle's left tackle situation: Charles Cross reportedly suffered a high ankle sprain and is likely to miss time. His availability matters against a Chicago defense getting Montez Sweat back from suspension. That's a protection matchup worth circling. 3. Chicago gets extra recovery time: The Bears played Thursday in Week 7. Seattle played Sunday night. Both now prepare for Monday Night Football, giving Chicago three additional days between games. 4. Seattle's backfield could get reinforcements: Zach Charbonnet is expected to practice fully as he works toward his season debut, while Jadarian Price is also nearing a return. Neither should be assumed available yet, but both are worth monitoring throughout the week. 5. Primetime prowess: Both teams have had success in island games. The Bears are 7-1 against the spread in primetime under second-year head coach Ben Johnson. Meanwhile, Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has won eight straight primetime games for Seattle and Minnesota by an average of 11.8 points per game. Chicago also has extra rest after beating New England last Thursday, giving Caleb Williams more time to prepare for a demanding matchup. The Bears have more weaponry than the Chiefs, including the league's best rushing offense. The visitors will put up a fight and keep this close. But the Seahawks have a dominant defense that translates at home better than anywhere else. A costly Williams turnover will define the night. The outcome of the game might hinge on the other side of the ball, where Sam Darnold and the Seahawks are hoping to avoid the backbreaking mistakes that could give Chicago life. With Seattle getting the pieces in place to firm up its run game, the defending champs might have the edge. Caleb Williams is playing out of his mind, making throws that aren't even possible in a video game. The same can't be said for Sam Darnold, who has been riding the struggle bus this season. Seattle's defense can shut down even the best offenses, but this Johnson-coached unit is a different beast. away.blurb: Muhammad picked up a toe injury against the New England Patriots in Week 7 while Monangai has been out since Week 4 with toe/thumb injuries of his own. Jackson was in a walking boot coming out of Week 7 whereas Edwards has been out since Week 6 with a hamstring injuries. Getting linebackers TJ Edwards and D’Marco Jackson back would be a boon. Both have been crucial leaders for the defense on the field. Having both available would make the Bears more consistent throughout the entire game. The Chicago Bears won’t release their first Week 8 injury report until Thursday. But on Tuesday, the franchise began their preperations for a difficult Monday Night Football battle against the Seattle Seahawks . When kickoff happens, the Bears are hoping to have as much of their roster healthy as possible. That wasn’t the case to start practice though, via Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune. “RB Kyle Monangai and CB Malik Muhammad were not spotted when practice was open to media,” Biggs wrote. “LBs D’Marco Jackson & TJ Edwards did participate. Jackson had a boot on his right foot last Thursday night.” As the week goes on, Chicago’s injury statues will become more clear. But Tuesday’s session carries weight as well. How Chicago Bears injuries affect Week 8 The Seahawks enter Week 8 with the sixth-best run defense in the NFL, allowing 89.4 yards per game. They just bottled Kansas City Chiefs star Kenneth Walker up for 36 yards on 14 carries in Week 6. Prior to his injury, Monangai averaged 5.4 yards per carry. He turned 60 carries into 324 yards and three touchdowns overall. While the Bears are confident in D’Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson, Monangai adds a different speaking to that running back room. In that Seahawks-Chiefs battle, Seattle receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 150 yards and a touchdown. Not many cornerbacks in the league can stop him. But not having Muhammad on the field would only lower Chicago’s ceiling on a secondary that has already been stumbling. The Bears will have more info as the week goes on. However, the number of players in the last two categories cannot exceed 10 total players. Teams can elevate up to two practice squad players for each game, but they can still only have 48 players active on game day. After the game, the elevated player(s) will revert to the practice squad. A player can be elevated up to three times, but if he's needed after that, the team would be required to sign him to the 53-man active roster. Players on practice squads are free agents who can be signed to another team's active roster. A player's current club can't block him from leaving; they can only make a counteroffer to keep him. Ultimately, it's the player's decision. If a player is signed away, his new team must keep him on its 53-man roster for three weeks, but if he's released, he'll revert to his previous team. Players signed to another active roster are also guaranteed three weeks' salary. A practice squad player can't sign with his team's upcoming opponent unless he does so six days before the upcoming game or ten days prior if his team is on its bye week.
